title: [RFC][Feature]: First-class session id for conversation aware routing
author: karen-sy
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

# vLLM Session Identity Roadmap

This plan is for plumbing session-aware identity into vLLM such that it is available for:
(1) consumption by external routing / serving frameworks. **This proposal is specifically for Dynamo integration**.
(2) vLLM-internal scheduling optimizations for agentic workflows

## Goal

Dynamo already extracts session identity from headers into `PreprocessedRequest.agent_context.session_id` and can use it in the Dynamo router. The missing piece is that vLLM needs a typed request-level session identity that engine internals, KV connectors, cache policy, or schedulers can consume without overloading `request_id` or hiding identity in `SamplingParams.extra_args`.

The target flow is:

```text
X-Dynamo-Session-ID / normalized agent session header
  -> Dynamo AgentContext.session_id
  -> Dynamo router session-aware behavior
  -> vLLM typed request-level session identity
  -> vLLM KV/cache/scheduler/connectors can optionally consume it
```

This is deliberately not:

```text
Dynamo session routing
  -> vLLM router feature
```

vLLM should receive stable request metadata. Dynamo should continue to own cluster-level routing.

## Current Context

- vLLM PR `vllm-project/vllm#46547` and commit [aac37e94](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/aac37e94ccae81382423f0449c5ed52f27f24fab#diff-60dbf8f976bb75c15f59e23e8c760dff094523375c9ef90cf78e1264c7f101a9) is the current vLLM-side workaround. They plumb `session_id` from HTTP headers `X-Session-ID` or `X-Correlation-ID` as `SamplingParams.extra_args["session_id"]` and forward that into Mooncake metadata.
- SGLang PR `sgl-project/sglang#29436` is useful reference for making `session_id` request-level engine state.
- `request_id` remains per-request and should keep its existing lifecycle semantics for aborts, output routing, scheduler maps, and request-local bookkeeping.
- `session_id` is stable across related requests in one conversation, agent run, or session.

## Proposal

Add a first-class scalar `session_id: str | None` to vLLM's request path.

The key design rule is:

```python
request.session_id
```

not:

```python
request.sampling_params.extra_args["session_id"]
```

`SamplingParams.extra_args["session_id"]` can remain a temporary compatibility input for existing experimental users, but it should not be the stable engine contract.

## Ingress Paths

There are two distinct ways session identity can reach vLLM.

When a client calls vLLM directly:

```text
OpenAI body session_id or HTTP X-Session-ID
  -> vLLM OpenAI serving layer
  -> vLLM EngineCoreRequest.session_id
  -> vLLM Request.session_id
```

When a client calls Dynamo first:

```text
HTTP X-Dynamo-Session-ID / normalized agent session header
  -> Dynamo AgentContext.session_id
  -> Dynamo router
  -> Dynamo vLLM backend calls vLLM with session_id=<AgentContext.session_id>
  -> vLLM EngineCoreRequest.session_id
  -> vLLM Request.session_id
```

The Dynamo bridge carries Dynamo's already-normalized session identity into vLLM. vLLM does not read the original client HTTP header in that path because it is behind Dynamo and receives an internal backend call.

## vLLM Public Ingress

Add optional `session_id` to the OpenAI-compatible request models:

```text
vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py
vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py
vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py
```

Suggested field:

```python
session_id: str | None = Field(
    default=None,
    description=(
        "Stable session identity shared by related requests. Unlike request_id, "
        "this value is expected to remain stable across multiple requests in "
        "the same conversation or agent session."
    ),
)
```

Resolve the effective session id in the serving layer, not inside `SamplingParams`:

```text
vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py
vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py
vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/batch_serving.py
vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py
vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py
```

Suggested precedence:

```text
request.session_id
  > X-Session-ID
  > X-Correlation-ID, if maintainers want to preserve compatibility with PR #46547
  > request.vllm_xargs["session_id"], as temporary compatibility only
```

Maintainer sanity checks:

- Should `X-Correlation-ID` be accepted at all, or should vLLM use only `X-Session-ID`?
- Should body `session_id` always win over headers?
- Should conflicting body/header/xargs values be ignored by precedence or rejected?

## vLLM Engine API

Add `session_id` beside existing non-sampling request controls like `priority`, `trace_headers`, and `data_parallel_rank`:

```text
vllm/engine/protocol.py
vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py
vllm/v1/engine/llm_engine.py
vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py
vllm/v1/engine/__init__.py
vllm/v1/request.py
```

Expected shape:

```python
AsyncLLM.generate(..., session_id: str | None = None)
AsyncLLM.add_request(..., session_id: str | None = None)
LLMEngine.add_request(..., session_id: str | None = None)
InputProcessor.process_inputs(..., session_id: str | None = None)
EngineCoreRequest.session_id: str | None
Request.session_id: str | None
```

Where `EngineCoreRequest` is converted into internal `Request`, copy the field:

```text
EngineCoreRequest.session_id -> Request.session_id
```

The current vLLM path includes:

```text
vllm/v1/engine/core.py
vllm/v1/request.py
```

For parallel sampling / child requests, preserve the parent request's `session_id` on every child request. `request_id` should still remain unique per child request.

For beam search, preserve the same `session_id` across the generated one-token subrequests:

```text
vllm/entrypoints/generate/beam_search/online.py
```

## vLLM Native / Offline API

The first PR can expose `session_id` through engine APIs and OpenAI serving first. Ask maintainers whether native/offline callers should also get parity immediately.

Possible follow-up surfaces:

```text
vllm/entrypoints/llm.py
vllm/inputs/engine.py
vllm/inputs/llm.py
vllm/inputs/preprocess.py
```

Two plausible native/offline designs:

- Add a `session_id: list[str | None] | None` argument to `LLM.generate`, analogous to per-prompt `priority`.
- Allow `session_id` in `EngineInput`, analogous to `cache_salt`.

Do not include this in the first patch unless maintainers ask for direct/offline parity.

## vLLM Rust Server / Engine-Core Client

Mirror the field in the Rust request path if the Rust server/client path is in scope:

```text
rust/src/server/src/utils.rs
rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/chat_completions/types.rs
rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/chat_completions/convert.rs
rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/completions/types.rs
rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/completions/convert.rs
rust/src/server/src/routes/inference/generate/convert.rs
rust/src/server/src/routes/tokenize/types.rs
rust/src/server/src/grpc/convert.rs
rust/src/text/src/request.rs
rust/src/text/src/lower.rs
rust/src/chat/src/request.rs
rust/src/chat/src/lib.rs
rust/src/llm/src/request.rs
rust/src/engine-core-client/src/protocol/request.rs
```

`rust/src/engine-core-client/src/protocol/request.rs` is especially important because it defines the Rust-side `EngineCoreRequest` that serializes compatibly with Python's `EngineCoreRequest`.

Add the new field with a default so older callers that omit it keep working:

```rust
#[serde(default)]
pub session_id: Option<String>,
```

In Rust HTTP/OpenAI lowering, use the same effective precedence as Python:

```text
request.session_id
  > X-Session-ID
  > X-Correlation-ID
  > request.vllm_xargs["session_id"]
```

The gRPC proto can be handled as a follow-up if maintainers want body-level gRPC parity. In the first patch, the Rust gRPC path can leave `session_id` unset unless the proto is already being changed for adjacent work.

## vLLM Consumers

Move consumers toward:

```python
request.session_id
```

and away from:

```python
request.sampling_params.extra_args["session_id"]
```

For the Mooncake work from PR `#46547`, the relevant files are:

```text
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/data.py
```

The first consumer update can use:

```python
session_id = request.session_id
if session_id is None:
    session_id = request.sampling_params.extra_args.get("session_id")
```

The fallback should be treated as temporary compatibility for older `vllm_xargs` callers.

## vLLM Tests

Add focused tests for:

- OpenAI body `session_id` is accepted for chat, completions, and responses.
- `X-Session-ID` is accepted by the OpenAI serving path.
- Header/body/xargs precedence is deterministic.
- `EngineCoreRequest.session_id` survives serialization and reaches `Request.session_id`.
- Parallel sampling children preserve `session_id` while retaining distinct request ids.
- Beam search subrequests preserve `session_id`.
- Mooncake metadata receives the typed `request.session_id` once consumers are updated.
- Existing `extra_args` / `vllm_xargs` behavior is not broken.

Likely test areas:

```text
tests/entrypoints/openai/
tests/v1/engine/
tests/v1/worker/
rust/src/engine-core-client/src/tests/
rust/src/server/src/routes/tests.rs
rust/src/server/src/grpc/tests.rs, if gRPC body-level parity is included
```

## vLLM Maintainer Questions

- Should vLLM accept `X-Correlation-ID` as a session identity input at all, or should this PR use only `X-Session-ID`?
- Is the desired precedence `request.session_id > X-Session-ID > X-Correlation-ID > request.vllm_xargs["session_id"]`? (see `serving.py` `_get_session_id()`)
- Should conflicting body/header/xargs values be ignored by precedence or rejected with a clear error?
- Should native/offline `LLM.generate` expose `session_id` in this PR, or should direct/offline API parity be a follow-up?
- Should PR 1 include the Rust frontend HTTP/OpenAI surface, or should it only add Python ingress plus the shared typed engine/protocol plumbing and leave Rust frontend parity to a separate Rust frontend PR?
- If Rust frontend HTTP/OpenAI parity is included, should it mirror the Python body/header/xargs precedence exactly?
- Should gRPC body-level `session_id` be added now, or should the Rust gRPC converter leave `session_id` unset until a proto follow-up?

## Dynamo Follow-Up

Current Dynamo behavior:

Relevant PRs:

- [ai-dynamo/dynamo#10875](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/10875) is the merged implementation for header-based session affinity and the `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` behavior below.

```text
X-Dynamo-Session-ID
  -> AgentContext.session_id
  -> SessionAffinityId
```

These two Dynamo objects have different lifecycles and consumers:

```text
AgentContext.session_id
  -> stored in request Context under AGENT_CONTEXT_CONTEXT_KEY
  -> copied by preprocessor into PreprocessedRequest.agent_context
  -> visible to router/backend request logic

SessionAffinityId
  -> stored in request Context under SESSION_AFFINITY_CONTEXT_KEY
  -> consumed directly by session-affinity router/coordinator
  -> not copied into PreprocessedRequest.agent_context
```

Native agent headers, such as Codex `session-id`, Claude Code `x-claude-code-session-id`, and OpenCode `x-session-id`, currently populate `AgentContext.session_id`. They do not populate `SessionAffinityId`; hard session affinity is tied to the canonical `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` header.

The missing bridge is from Dynamo's backend-visible request identity into vLLM. Once vLLM has a typed field, Dynamo should pass `agent_context.session_id` into vLLM's typed `session_id` field instead of using `SamplingParams.extra_args["session_id"]` as the primary path.

Python vLLM backend:

```text
components/src/dynamo/vllm/handlers.py
components/src/dynamo/vllm/llm_engine.py
```

Add a small helper:

```python
def _session_id_for_vllm(request: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    agent_context = request.get("agent_context")
    if isinstance(agent_context, Mapping):
        value = agent_context.get("session_id")
        if isinstance(value, str) and value:
            return value
    return None
```

Then pass it on every vLLM `generate` call:

```python
self.engine_client.generate(
    ...,
    session_id=_session_id_for_vllm(request),
)
```

Important call sites:

```text
components/src/dynamo/vllm/handlers.py
components/src/dynamo/vllm/llm_engine.py
```

Cover the normal generation path, decode worker path, prefill worker path, and local engine path.

Rust vLLM backend:

```text
lib/vllm-rs-backend/src/convert.rs
```

Map:

```rust
request.agent_context.as_ref().map(|ctx| ctx.session_id.clone())
```

into the vLLM `GenerateRequest` / `EngineCoreRequest` typed `session_id` field.

Add tests in:

```text
components/src/dynamo/vllm/tests/test_vllm_worker_handler.py
components/src/dynamo/vllm/tests/test_vllm_engine.py
lib/vllm-rs-backend/src/convert.rs
```

Test that `agent_context.session_id` reaches the engine call and that unrelated `extra_args` are preserved.

## Dynamo Compatibility Choice

During migration, Dynamo can optionally also populate `sampling_params.extra_args["session_id"]` for older vLLM versions. Avoid making that the long-term behavior.

If both a caller-provided vLLM `session_id` and Dynamo `agent_context.session_id` exist and disagree, prefer one explicit policy:

- strict policy: reject with a clear error
- permissive policy: Dynamo `agent_context.session_id` wins because the router already used it

For consistency between router and backend, the strict policy is easier to reason about.

## Future Extension

If vLLM maintainers want a broader home for non-sampling request metadata, this scalar field can later grow into a typed object, for example:

```python
class RequestMetadata(msgspec.Struct, omit_defaults=True):
    session_id: str | None = None
```

In that design, public request bodies can still expose top-level `session_id`, while the serving layer lowers it into `RequestMetadata(session_id=...)`. Avoid naming the public OpenAI field `metadata`; OpenAI-compatible APIs already use `metadata` for user/application metadata, especially Responses.

Potential future metadata fields could include tenant, cache namespace, parent session, session finality, or cache lineage. Do not include those in the first session-id PR unless maintainers explicitly ask for a broader metadata object.

## Suggested PR Split

### vLLM PR 1: Typed Session Identity Plumbing https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48048

- Add `session_id` as typed request-level state.
- Include OpenAI ingress, Python engine path, Rust server/client path, and tests.
- Keep legacy `vllm_xargs["session_id"]` only as compatibility input.
- Do not introduce new scheduling/cache policy.

### vLLM PR 2: Consumers Use Typed Session Identity

- Update Mooncake / KV connector consumers to read `request.session_id`.
- Preserve temporary fallback to `extra_args["session_id"]` if maintainers want migration compatibility.
- Add focused connector tests.

### Dynamo PR: Bridge AgentContext To vLLM

- Python backend: pass `agent_context.session_id` into vLLM generate calls.
- Rust backend: lower `PreprocessedRequest.agent_context.session_id` into vLLM `GenerateRequest`.
- Add tests proving Dynamo does not need to smuggle session identity through `SamplingParams.extra_args`.

## Non-Goals

- Do not add conversation-aware routing to vLLM's router.
- Do not overload `request_id`.
- Do not require SGLang-style `/open_session` lifecycle semantics.
- Do not make `SamplingParams.extra_args["session_id"]` the stable contract.
- Do not plumb Dynamo-only agent hints directly into vLLM unless there is a separate vLLM design discussion for them.


### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

title: [RFC]: Confident Decoding — entropy-guided intermediate-layer logits selection
author: zhoubiansining
body:
# [RFC]: Confident Decoding — entropy-guided intermediate-layer logits selection

## Summary

We propose adding **Confident Decoding** to vLLM: a training-free decoding strategy that dynamically selects logits from near-final intermediate layers instead of always using the final layer. Layer selection is guided by prediction entropy (conservative backward search for the first entropy valley closest to the final layer).

This is the inference implementation accompanying our paper:

> **Deeper is Not Always Better: Mitigating the Alignment Tax via Confident Layer Decoding**  
> Xuanming Zhang, Sining Zhoubian, Yuxuan Chen, et al.  
> arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21906

The paper shows consistent gains on challenging reasoning benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, Omni-MATH, HLE) across dense and MoE LLMs, with zero memory overhead and <2% latency increase.

## Motivation

Standard autoregressive decoding always uses logits from the **final** transformer layer. Our work reveals a recurring **Guess-Refine-Perturb** dynamic: early layers form coarse guesses, intermediate layers refine reasoning-relevant semantics, and final layers can perturb refined predictions toward generic or alignment-preferred tokens.

Confident Decoding bypasses harmful final-layer perturbations by selecting the most confident near-final layer at each token position.

## Proposed API

Enabled via `--additional-config` (no recompilation required):

```bash
vllm serve /path/to/model \
  --additional-config '{
    "enable_multi_layer_entropy_selection": true,
    "select_method": "trough",
    "p": 1.0,
    "trough_max_backtrack_layers": 10
  }'
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enable_multi_layer_entropy_selection` | bool | `false` | Global switch |
| `select_method` | str | `"trough"` | Layer selection strategy (`trough`, `trough-m1`, `last-m8`, etc.) |
| `p` | float | `1.0` | Probability of using selected-layer logits; `0.0` = standard final-layer decoding |
| `trough_max_backtrack_layers` | int | `0` | Max layers to backtrack; `>0` uses this value; `<0` unlimited |
| `trough_backtrack_ratio` | float | `0.0` | Used when `trough_max_backtrack_layers == 0` |
| `trough_log_interval` | int | `0` | Periodic selection statistics logging; `0` disables |

## Technical Design

### CUDA graph compatibility

vLLM's CUDA graph capture covers the outer model wrapper. Mutating Python attributes or dynamic buffers inside compiled forward causes stale state on graph replay. Our design:

1. **Inner model** (compiled): collects raw candidate-layer hidden states only (similar to existing `aux_hidden_states`).
2. **Outer CausalLM wrapper** (eager): applies final norm to collected states and stores in shape-keyed buffers.
3. **Model runner** (eager): sets `_last_seq_len` and `_last_logits_indices` before `compute_logits`, keyed by CUDA graph batch shape.
4. **`compute_logits`**: batched `lm_head` over `[L*B, H]`, entropy computation, backward trough scan, gather selected logits.

### Selection algorithm (default `trough`)

1. Compute logits for all candidate layers in one batched `lm_head` call.
2. Compute per-token, per-layer prediction entropy.
3. Scan backward from the final candidate layer; continue while entropy decreases.
4. Stop at the first entropy increase (entropy valley closest to final layer).
5. Optionally mix with final-layer logits via probability `p`.

### Limitations (initial PR)

- Pipeline parallelism (`pp > 1`): disabled for correctness.
- Additional `lm_head` + entropy compute overhead per token (bounded by backtrack window).
- Some multimodal entry points (e.g. Qwen3-VL with deepstack) require separate integration.

## Proposed PR plan

We plan to land this in phases to keep reviews manageable:

| Phase | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| **PR 1** | `trough_utils.py`, v1 worker hooks, **Llama + Qwen3**, unit tests, `docs/features/confident_decoding.md` |
| **PR 2** | Gemma, Mixtral, MoE variants |
| **PR 3** | Multimodal entry points, DeepSeek, GPT-OSS |

Estimated core PR size: ~800 LOC (excluding model-family expansions).

## Validation plan

- **Unit tests**: `vectorized_entropy_select` layer selection logic; `compute_trough_layer_range`; `prepare_trough_layer_states` alignment.
- **Regression**: `p=0.0` produces identical outputs to standard final-layer decoding.
- **Deterministic check**: `select_method=last-mk` selects fixed layer index.
- **Integration**: small-model e2e generation smoke test.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is `additional_config` the preferred configuration surface, or should this become a first-class `VllmConfig` field?
2. Should we rename `enable_multi_layer_entropy_selection` → `enable_confident_decoding` for clarity (with backward-compatible alias)?
3. Any concerns about the CUDA graph buffer design vs. alternative approaches?

## References

- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21906
- Implementation prototype (vLLM 0.19.1 fork): https://github.com/zhoubiansining/vllm (branch `confident-dev`)

title: [RFC]: [ROCm][DistInf]: Distributed Inference (Disaggregated P/D + Wide-EP) CI Enablement on ROCm
author: lcskrishna
body:
### Motivation.

Distributed / disaggregated inference is now a first-class vLLM workload, but there is currently no upstream CI that continuously validates disaggregated P/D or Wide-EP on ROCm. 

As a result:
* Regressions in the ROCm disaggregated path (accuracy on PD, KV transfer, MoRI-IO connector, expert-parallel all2all) are only caught manually and late.
* The multi-node / RDMA code paths (prefill to decode KV push over RoCE NICs) get zero automated coverage, despite being the most fragile part of the stack.
* Accuracy drift undetected: no gating on end-to-end accuracy (e.g. GSM8K) for the disaggregated path.

## Summary
This RFC proposes establishing a dedicated Distributed Inference (DI) CI pipeline for ROCm/AMD GPUs in vLLM, covering disaggregated Prefill/Decode (P/D) serving with the MoRI-IO KV connector, in both TP and Wide Expert-Parallel (DP+EP) topologies, running on multi-node AMD clusters via Buildkite + Slurm.

The initial implementation is proposed in vLLM PR #47030. This RFC captures the broader plan, architecture, test matrix, staged rollout, infra requirements, and open design questions so the community can align on direction before we expand coverage and make the pipeline gating.

### Proposed Change.

### Overview
Add a self-contained DI CI harness under `.buildkite/amd-disagg/` (PR #47030) that:
- Stands up a full P/D topology (proxy/router + prefill + decode) on a multi-node AMD Slurm / spur allocation.
- Health-gates every server before sending traffic.
- Runs an end-to-end GSM8K accuracy check (and optionally a benchmark mode) through the disaggregated pipeline.
- Supports two modes via `WIDE_EP_MODE`:
  - `WIDE_EP_MODE=0` : general P/D with independent TP8 servers.
  - `WIDE_EP_MODE=1` : DP + Expert Parallelism (e.g. DP8/EP8/TP1, and 2P2D DP16/EP).
  
### Components (as in PR #47030)
- `vllm_disagg.sh` — launcher for proxy/router, prefill, decode; runs accuracy/bench.
- `cluster.sh` — single-sourced, per-cluster config (ports, topology, RDMA/NIC, MoRI env).
- `run-slurm-disagg-test.sh` — foreground Slurm submitter (the single command CI invokes).
- `run_xPyD_disagg.slurm` — the xPyD Slurm job (container launch, per-node image pull, cleanup).
- `pipeline.disagg.yaml` — Buildkite step snippet for the AMD DI test matrix.
- `models.yaml` — per-model, per-role (prefill/decode), per-mode flags.

### Proposed test matrix (initial to expanded)
| Stage | Topology | Parallelism | Connector | Router | Gate |

title: [RFC]: Optimizing Asynchronous Stream Serialization in OpenAI API Entrypoint
author: shujaSN
body:
### Motivation.

Currently, vLLM’s OpenAI-compatible API server processes incoming HTTP requests and handles request streaming on a unified FastAPI event loop. While this architecture performs exceptionally well for text-only inputs, it introduces severe performance regressions under concurrent multimodal workloads (e.g., high-resolution Vision-Language Models or video input processing).

When a request containing large base64-encoded images or video frames hits the /v1/chat/completions endpoint, the payload validation (via Pydantic), base64 decoding, and initial tensor formatting happen in a way that blocks the main asynchronous event loop.

During local profiling under a simulated load of 50 concurrent connections, processing a request with multiple high-res image inputs blocks the FastAPI event loop for up to 42ms to 65ms. Because the AsyncLLMEngine scheduling loop relies on this same event loop to fetch tokens and step the engine, this starvation directly causes severe spikes in Inter-Token Latency (ITL) and Time-to-First-Token (TTFB) across all concurrent requests on the instance, completely neutralizing continuous batching efficiency.

### Proposed Change.

I propose decoupling the heavy ingress payload ingestion from the critical engine scheduling path by refactoring the vllm/entrypoints/openai layer:

**Offloaded Ingress Processing:** Move base64 decoding, multimodal payload parsing, and structural validation entirely off the main FastAPI event loop into an asynchronous worker pool using a configured ProcessPoolExecutor or dedicated CPU ingress threads.

**Zero-Copy Shared Memory IPC: I**nstead of serializing massive raw image/video arrays across process boundaries via standard Python pipes (which introduces a second serialization bottleneck to the engine process), utilize a shared-memory buffer (multiprocessing.shared_memory) or zero-copy memory views. The API entrypoint will write the processed multimodal tensors to shared memory and pass only lightweight memory references/metadata pointers to the LLMEngine queue.

**Refactored serving_chat.py:** Update the request handler in vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py to handle these asynchronous memory allocations cleanly, ensuring deterministic cleanup of shared memory blocks immediately after the engine completes prefill processing.

This change isolates text-only streams from being penalised by concurrent heavy multimodal payloads and ensures the engine scheduler is consistently saturated.

### Feedback Period.

10 Days. I would highly appreciate feedback from the core maintainers on how this interacts with the long-term V1 engine migration and architecture.

### CC List.

@simon-mo @zhuohan123

### Any Other Things.

I have a localized micro-benchmark script using k6 and yappi that reliably reproduces this event-loop starvation under multimodal loads. I can share the flame graphs and performance profiles in a follow-up comment if requested.

If the core maintainers agree with this architectural direction, I am prepared to open a draft PR implementing the decoupled ProcessPoolExecutor ingress path for review.

title: [RFC]: Remove Group Activation Ordering (actorder=group) Support from vLLM and Compression Libraries
author: kylesayrs
body:
## Motivation

This RFC proposes the removal of runtime group activation ordering (actorder) support from vLLM, compressed-tensors, and llm-compressor. This affects GPTQ quantized models (W4A16, W8A16, and other WNA16 variants) that use `actorder=group` during quantization.

**Key motivations:**

1. **Limited kernel support**: Modern high-performance kernels (Humming, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer) do not support `g_idx`-based runtime reordering. Supporting actorder limits adoption of faster kernels.

2. **Performance cost**: Group actorder incurs ~2.5% runtime overhead (data from [PR #8135](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8135))

3. **Better alternatives exist**: Weight-based (static) activation ordering provides:
   - Similar accuracy (73.54% vs 72.63% on GSM-8K from PR #8135)
   - Zero runtime performance penalty
   - Full compatibility with all kernel backends

4. **Code complexity**: Supporting group actorder adds significant complexity across vLLM (W4A16, W8A16, MoE variants), compressed-tensors, and llm-compressor.

## Proposed Change

**Two-phase approach:**

### Phase 1: Remove from Compression Libraries (Immediate)
- **compressed-tensors**: Remove `ActivationOrdering.GROUP` and `ActivationOrdering.DYNAMIC`
- **llm-compressor**: Remove `actorder=group` option from quantization recipes
- **Impact**: Only affects new model creation; existing models unaffected
- **Benefit**: Prevents new models from using this feature

### Phase 2: Remove from vLLM Inference (Discussion)
**This RFC seeks community input on whether to proceed with Phase 2**

If approved, would remove:
- `weight_g_idx` parameter loading and handling
- `has_g_idx` flags and conditional logic in quantization schemes
- Runtime column reordering in Marlin and other kernels
- ~300-500 lines of actorder handling code across vLLM
- Support from: `compressed_tensors_wNa16.py`, `compressed_tensors_w4a8_fp8.py`, MoE implementations, legacy GPTQ

**What remains**: Static activation reordering algorithm (the algorithm that reorders weights during quantization). This becomes the default - weights are saved in reordered form with zero runtime cost.

## Open Questions for Community

1. **Should Phase 2 proceed?** Or maintain backward compatibility indefinitely?

2. **If yes, what timeline?**
   - Deprecation period (1, 2, or 3+ releases)?
   - Should we maintain a legacy branch/Docker image?

3. **Migration support**:
   - Provide detection tool for affected models?
   - Automated re-quantization scripts?
   - Coordinate with HuggingFace to update public models?

4. **Kernel interfaces**:
   - Remove `g_idx` parameters entirely or keep as ignored for compatibility?
   - Remove legacy GPTQ support entirely or only actorder feature?

## Detailed Design Document

Full RFC with background, alternatives considered, and implementation details: [docs/design/remove_gptq_actorder.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/kylesayrs/deepseek-ct/docs/design/remove_gptq_actorder.md)

## Impact

**Affected models** (Phase 2 only):
- GPTQ W4A16/W8A16 with `actorder=group` or `desc_act=True`
- Compressed-tensors models with `ActivationOrdering.GROUP`
- Some older TheBloke GPTQ quantizations
- Estimated scope: Small subset, most modern models use static reordering

**Benefits**:
- Performance: Eliminate 2-3% overhead
- Kernel compatibility: Enable Humming and future kernels
- Code simplification: Remove ~300-500 lines
- Reduced testing surface and maintenance burden
- Easier cross-platform porting (ROCm, TPU, NPU)

## References

- Original actorder PR: [#8135](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8135)
- Humming kernel PRs: [#46390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46390), [#42997](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42997)
- GPTQ paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.17323

title: [RFC]: StructuredOutputManager x Speculative Decoding Refactor
author: yzong-rh
body:
### Motivation.

Simplify the contract between `Scheduler`, grammar backend, and `StructuredOutputManager`, especially when speculative decoding is used.

`StructuredOutputManager` exists because constrained decoding often doesn't kick in until a model has finished reasoning. With speculative decoding, grammar-invalid draft tokens need to be rejected, draft tokens need to temporarily advance grammar state to generate bitmasks, rejected draft tokens should not advance grammar state. Reasoning end boundary can also fall in the middle of the draft token window, so only draft tokens after said boundary should advance grammar state.

`Scheduler` and the `StructuredOutputManager` need to do a careful dance to make this is all correct. This leads to some bugs such as [#34650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34650) -- only recently fixed thanks to [#44297](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44297).

```
Per request inside a scheduler step
1. StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)                         # Should we constrain some draft tokens?
   Grammar.validate_tokens(draft tokens)                                   # Reject grammar invalid draft tokens
2. StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...)                            # Generate bitmasks for the draft tokens
3. Verifier runs
4. StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)                         # Should we constrain some draft token? 
   StructuredOutputManager.trim_reasoning_for_advance(verified tokens)     # Trim the draft tokens that are not constrained
   Grammar.accept_tokens(verified tokens)                                  # Advance grammar state
```

In fact, speculative decoding x constrained decoding remains fragile / subtly incorrect:
1. ~~`StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)` treats STRUCTURAL_TAG vs other constraint types differently. It defers non STRUCTURAL_TAG constraints. [#44297](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44297) only fix the strict tool calling case (which uses STRUCTURAL_TAG); [#34650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34650) is still unfixed for JSON, REGEX, and other constraint types.~~ Fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44993
2. ~~`StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)` also doesn't answer "should we constrain some draft tokens?" reliably. It incorrectly infers the draft token window from `num_output_placeholders`.~~ Fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44993
3. `Grammar.validate_tokens(draft_tokens)` only works on a best effort basis -- it doesn't validate any draft token unless all draft tokens should be constrained. We rely on `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...)` and rejection sampling to discard grammer-invalid tokens.

### Proposed Change.

Let `StructuredOutputManager` handle the token validation and grammar advancement.

Remove:
- `StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)`
- `StructuredOutputManager.trim_reasoning_for_advance(verified tokens)`

Add:
- `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens(draft tokens)`
- `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens(verified tokens)`

```
Per request inside a scheduler step
1. StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens(draft tokens)
2. StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...)
3. Verifier runs
4. StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens(verified tokens)
```

Internally, `validate_tokens()`, `grammar_bitmask()`, and `accept_tokens()` all use the same `_get_constraint_start()` helper to determine whether and where draft tokens should be constrained and grammar state advanced.

Concretly, `_get_constraint_start()` computes the first token that should be grammar-constrained.

- `validate_tokens()` preserves any unconstrained prefix and validates only the constrained suffix.
- `grammar_bitmask()` emits unconstrained bitmaks before the boundary and constrained bitmasks after it.
- `accept_tokens()` advances the grammar state only on the constrained suffix only

This gives a simpler mental model for the system. The scheduler is responsible for request lifecycle and token plumbing. `StructuredOutputManager` is responsible for draft token validation, bitmask generation, and grammar backends.

~100 insertions, ~200 deletions of changes excluding test updates.

~~Would fix issues like: #34650 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43388~~

title: [RFC]: GLM-5.x thinking_token_budget defaults and regression tests
author: AlanJager
body:
### Motivation

GLM-5.x models can spend the whole completion budget in the reasoning phase when thinking is enabled by default. This makes OpenAI-compatible chat/tool-calling flows difficult to use unless the caller explicitly disables thinking or sets a small `thinking_token_budget`.

In a local vLLM 0.24.0 deployment, `thinking_token_budget` already works with GLM-5.2 when serving with:

```bash
vllm serve <glm-5.2-fp8> \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --chat-template-content-format string
```

A small budget prevented the response from being consumed entirely by reasoning and still allowed streaming tool calls to work.

Related prior issues/PRs:

- #26091 (`[Feature]: GLM thinking budget`) is closed as stale.
- #34827 (`Support thinking budget for reasoning models (e.g., GLM-4.5V)`) is closed as stale.
- #20859 added the hard thinking-token limit.
- #46727 is tracking Model Runner V2 support.

This issue is not asking for a duplicate implementation of the generic budget mechanism. It is asking whether the project wants GLM-5.x-specific regression coverage, recommended/default budget guidance, and possibly model-family defaults or documentation.

### Observed behavior

Using a short Chinese final-answer prompt with `max_tokens=192`:

```text
no thinking_token_budget:
  completion_tokens: 192
  reasoning chars:   344
  content chars:     0
  finish_reason:     length

thinking_token_budget=16:
  reasoning chars:   31
  content chars:     287
  finish_reason:     length

thinking_token_budget=32:
  completion_tokens: 154 in one run, 87 in a two-sentence run
  reasoning tokens:  32
  content tokens:    53 in the token-inspected run
  finish_reason:     stop
```

With `return_token_ids=true`, the `thinking_token_budget=32` run had the expected layout:

```text
0-31   reasoning tokens        32 tokens
32     </think>                1 token
33-85  final content           53 tokens
86     stop token              1 token
```

For this GLM-5.2 tokenizer:

```text
<think>   -> 154841
</think>  -> 154842
stop      -> 154827
```

A streaming tool-call request with `thinking_token_budget=16`, `tool_choice="auto"`, `--reasoning-parser glm45`, and `--tool-call-parser glm47` produced normal OpenAI-compatible chunks:

```json
{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{"type":"function","index":0,"function":{"name":"get_current_time","arguments":"{}"}}]}}
```

and ended with:

```json
{"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}
```

### Question / proposed direction

Would maintainers prefer any of the following?

1. Add GLM-5.x documentation recommending conservative `thinking_token_budget` ranges, for example:
   - tool / agent / MCP-style calls: `16` or `32`, or disable thinking
   - ordinary short QA: `32` to `64`
   - complex reasoning: caller-specified, higher values such as `128+`
2. Add regression tests showing that GLM-5.x + `glm45` respects `thinking_token_budget` without consuming all `max_tokens`.
3. Add tool-calling regression tests ensuring a budgeted reasoning phase still transitions cleanly to `delta.tool_calls` and `finish_reason="tool_calls"`.
4. Add a model-family default or server-side option for GLM-5.x deployments so users do not have to pass the budget on every request.

### Draft test plan

A draft patch could add tests around these cases:

- Non-streaming chat with `thinking_token_budget=32`:
  - `message.reasoning` re-encodes to `<= 32` tokens.
  - returned `token_ids` contain the reasoning tokens followed by `</think>`.
  - `message.content` is non-empty.
  - `finish_reason` is not `length` when `max_tokens` is sufficient.
- Boundary values:
  - `thinking_token_budget=0` should be defined clearly: either no reasoning or rejected/documented behavior.
  - very small values such as `8` should not leak partial reasoning scaffold into `content`.
- Streaming tool call:
  - request includes `thinking_token_budget`, `tools`, and `tool_choice="auto"`.
  - stream emits `delta.reasoning` first, then `delta.tool_calls`.
  - final chunk uses `finish_reason="tool_calls"`.
  - `</think>` is not inserted into tool arguments.
- Compatibility matrix:
  - V0/V1/MRV2 if applicable.
  - speculative decoding on/off if applicable.
  - stream/non-stream.

If this direction is acceptable, I can prepare a draft PR with the above regression tests and docs notes.

title: [RFC]: Per-request effective proposal lengths for adaptive speculative decoding
author: LJX-xixi
body:
### Motivation.

### Current state

vLLM has established support for adapting a batch-uniform speculation depth.
Dynamic SD (#32374) profiles position-level acceptance and ITL offline and
selects a per-step uniform K by goodput at runtime (currently EAGLE-1), and
#45953 extended it to work with full CUDA graphs. Separately, #36657 / #35301
proposed confidence-threshold early exit for drafting, deliberately
batch-uniform: outputs stay fixed-width `[batch_size, K]` with zero padding,
and the PR notes that "a per-request policy would be more efficient but
requires variable-length draft outputs and more complex KV-cache bookkeeping."

The interface question addressed here is orthogonal to all of the above:
representing different effective proposal lengths across requests within the
same batch.

### The gap

Acceptance behavior varies both across workloads and across requests within a
batch. With `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` on Qwen3-4B, mean accepted
length is 6.12 on GSM8K and 3.63 on MT-Bench (block size 7, matching Table 1
of the DSpark paper, arXiv:2607.05147). More importantly for this RFC,
instrumented MT-Bench batches produce per-request confident-prefix lengths
spanning the full 0..7 range within a single step, for example
`[7, 4, 0, 7, 2, 1, 0, 0]`. Accepted-length numbers include the
target-generated bonus token, following the DSpark paper's protocol, whereas
proposal lengths here count draft tokens only.

A uniform K, however well chosen, pays for this within-batch spread either in
wasted verification (K too long for cold requests) or lost acceptance (K too
short for hot ones). The missing piece is not a policy but a contract:
per-request proposal-length metadata and its semantics across the proposer,
model runner, scheduler accounting, async scheduling, and metrics. This is
also the interface boundary left unresolved by several earlier
adaptive-speculation attempts (#28693, #26504, #44885, #43522).

Observed behavior in our prototype, based on vLLM main at `b8c7c8653`:
modifying the per-request `DraftTokenIds` lists changes effective truncation
when async scheduling is disabled, but does not change verification or
scheduler accounting on the default async path, whose draft-token feedback is
consulted for structured-output validation. This is consistent with the
fixed-shape design choice documented in #35301.

### Prototype evidence

As a concrete first consumer we wired the DSpark confidence head, which
DeepSeek ships in the released checkpoints and vLLM currently skips at load
time with the comment `confidence_head is not wired into inference yet`
(`qwen3_dspark.py`). The head is a single `Linear(hidden + markov_rank -> 1)`;
the Markov embedding it consumes is already computed inside
`DSparkSpeculator`'s sequential sampling loop, so the confidence score
requires one lightweight linear projection per draft position. The prototype
preserves fixed tensor shapes and runs under the graph mode used in our test
setup; full compatibility with the default async CUDA-graph path is part of
the proposed infrastructure work, not claimed here. Per-request confident
lengths come out as an int32 tensor copied to host outside capture. A
reference branch with the patch and measurement scripts is linked below.

Reference branch: 
https://github.com/LJX-xixi/vllm/tree/per-request-proposal-lengths-ref
(five focused changes plus unit tests; measurement scripts and raw numbers available on request.)

### Proposed Change.

### Proposed interface and semantics

We propose representing per-request proposal lengths logically, keeping
physical buffers fixed-shape.

For a decode step with maximum speculation depth `K`, the proposer may return:

* `draft_token_ids`: the fixed-shape `[R, K]` tensor, as today;
* `proposal_lengths`: an optional int32 vector `[R]` with
  `0 <= proposal_lengths[r] <= K`.

For request `r`, only the prefix `draft_token_ids[r, :proposal_lengths[r]]`
is semantically present. Positions beyond that prefix must not participate in
verification, KV-cache accounting, output-placeholder accounting, or
speculative-decoding metrics. When `proposal_lengths` is absent, the existing
uniform-K behavior is preserved bit-for-bit.

The length vector is bound to the exact in-flight batch that produced it; in
the async path it must not retroactively modify accounting for any other
batch. Whether a backend physically packs the valid prefixes or keeps padding
is an implementation choice; the interface defines only the logical lengths
and the accounting invariants. This intentionally reframes "variable-length
draft outputs" as a fixed-shape buffer plus a per-request logical length,
which is what our prototype implements.

The main design question we would like maintainer input on: should this
metadata extend Dynamic SD's existing machinery from #32374, or live as an
independent field on proposer/model-runner output consumed by scheduler
accounting? We have a working prototype of the second shape and will converge
on whichever boundary is preferred before opening the PR series:

1. `[Core][Spec Decode]` per-request proposal-length metadata, default
   behavior unchanged, sync and async paths tested, no policy attached.
2. `[Model][Spec Decode]` wire the Qwen3 DSpark confidence head as the first
   consumer, with an off-by-default minimal threshold and a small benchmark.
3. Policies as separate follow-ups.

### Non-goals

This RFC does not propose a default policy, and it makes no performance
claim. Honest measurement from the prototype: on Qwen3-4B on a single L20X up
to batch 64, confidence early stopping did not improve wall clock over fixed
full blocks at any threshold we tried; the DSpark backbone drafts the whole
block in one pass regardless of truncation, and in this regime per-step cost
is nearly flat in verified tokens while lost acceptance is paid in extra
decoding steps. These results show that per-request truncation is not
universally profitable: its value depends on the opportunity cost of
verification capacity, which may be higher for larger targets, saturated
engines, or other adaptive policies, and it is the prerequisite for any
per-request method (SpecDec++-style heads, or the per-request extension that
#35301 explicitly deferred). Accordingly, this RFC proposes an expressive
mechanism, not a performance claim or a policy recommendation; thresholds and
schedulers stay out of scope and default off.

### Feedback Period.

Two weeks (through July 24), or whatever the spec-decode maintainers prefer.

### CC List.

@ekagra-ranjan @jmamou

### Any Other Things.

### Related work

#32374 / #45953 (batch-level Dynamic SD), #36657 / #35301 (batch-mean
confidence early exit, fixed-width by design), RFC #46295 (MoE utility
budgeting, batch-level and complementary), #28693 / #26504 / #44885 / #43522
(earlier adaptive attempts), DeepSpec (github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSpec) for
the confidence head recipe, SpecDec++ (arXiv:2405.19715) for
acceptance-prediction heads.

Happy to open the reference branch as a draft PR immediately if that is
easier to review.
