title: [RFC]: Layerwise and Sparse KV cache offloading to support longer sequence length
author: zhangsicheng5
body:
## Motivation. In long sequence inference scenario, KV cache size has become one of the inference bottlenecks, arousing great interest in KV cache offloading. We also notice that KV cache offloading is especially efficient for sparse attention based model: Take [GLM-5.2](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.2) as an example, although we still need to store full KV cache, only topk (2048) of them are needed in sparse attention, this give us opportunity to save GPU memory usage by offloading the unused KV to host. Based on the layerwise KV cache offloading approach we proposed in RFC ([#33398](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33398)) and the sparse KV cache offloading approach we proposed in RFC ([#33980](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33980)), we now come up with a method that combines both these two approach, saving GPU memory usage in both prefill stage and decode stage. 1. **Layerwise KV cache offload & Prefill:** For prefill node (or prefill requests in pd-colocate), we use the layerwise KV cache offload. As explained in RFC ([#33398](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33398)), multiple layers share one KV cache buffer, each layer fully onload its KV cache into this shared buffer before attention forward, and release it after attention is done. Although we need to onload & offload full KV cache of each layer, we can use multiple device KV cache buffer to parallel computing and loading, and prefill stage is long enough to cover the loading time. According to our experiments, 2-4 KV cache buffers are enough to overlap most of the loading time with computing.
2. **Sparse KV cache offload & Decode:** For decode node (or decode requests in pd-colocate), we use the sparse KV cache offload. As explained in RFC ([#33398](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33398)), all KV cache are offloaded to host, each layer only onload its needed topk KV cache during attention forward. Since we only onload the topk KV, loading time is short enough to be used in decode stage. We can further optimize loading time by cache reuse: each step we store the needed topk KV in a device buffer, during the next step we can reuse the KV which are already on device, only the cache miss part need to be onload from host. Based on DeepSeek-V3.2, we achieve 80%-90% cache hit rate by using a device buffer size of 2 * topk.
Layerwise KV cache offloading can save KV cache GPU memory to $\frac{num\\_device\\_layers}{num\\_total\\_layers}$, and sparse KV cache offloading can save KV cache GPU memory usage to $\frac{indexer\\_cache\\_size}{kv\\_cache\\_size + indexer\\_cache\\_size}$ (Since indexer cache is not offloaded). By using these two offloading approach, we can save device memory usage in both prefill and decode. For example based on [GLM-5.2](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.2), we can save KV cache GPU memory usage up to 1/16 of original size, support up to 16x longer max_model_len or 16x larger batch_size. ## Proposed Change. ### KV cache management To support the layerwise KV offload and sparse KV offload above, we need some modification on the KV cache management. A. KV cache: Regardless of the model's layer number, we only allocate a fixed number of device KV cache buffers (currently we think 2-4 is enough). Needed for prefill. B. Indexer cache: All the indexer caches are kept on device. Needed for both prefill and decode. C. Topk buffer: A new device buffer to store the onloaded topk KV cache for each layer. Needed for decode. Topk buffer has a fixed size of n * topk, n == 1 meets the basic requirement of sparse attention, while we can also set n greater than 1 to improve cache hit rate. D. CPU KV cache: Host buffer to store the offloaded full KV caches of all layers.
Our first design use hybrid KV cache mode to manage the device KV cache and indexer cache, so that we can support KV offload in both PD disaggregate and PD co-locate scenario. However, considering the implementation of hybrid KV cache mode is complex and may lead to too much intrusive modification, we decide to support PD disaggregate scenerio first, in this case P nodes only need to allocate KV cache & indexer cache in a fixed ratio of available memory, and D nodes only need to allocate indexer cache. We can implement this without hybrid KV cache support and less modification is needed in model_runner. As for supporting KV offload in PD co-locate scenario, we might need more discussion in the future. ### Attention backend Based on the layerwise/sparse offload motivation and the KV cache data structure above, we need some modification on the current sparse attention backend. In prefill stage, we only use KV cache and indexer cache, the topk buffer is inactive. As explained in RFC ([#33398](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33398)), we can reuse the current KVConnector based KV offloading framework: make sure current layers' KV cache is already onloaded in `wait_for_layer_load` before attention forward, and start KV offload of current layer and KV onload of next layer in `save_kv_layer` after attention forward. Most of the other attention compute flow can keep unchanged.
In decode stage, we only use indexer cache and topk buffer, the original device KV cache is inactive. Some of the original compute flow need modification: First, after PreAttn(qkv_proj, norm, rope, etc.), we need to offload the new KV to CPU KV cache instead of writing them to original GPU KV cache. Second, based on the topk_idx from indexer, we need to onload needed topk KV from CPU KV cache to the topk buffer. To speedup h2d, we also perform cache reuse here, topk KV which are already in topk buffer don't need to be onloaded again. Third, we perform sparse attention based on topk buffer instead of original KV cache.
We might need a new sparse + offload attention backend to implement this. ### Offload backend The offload backend should provide following KV transfer interface for offloading: 1. `d2h_block(src_block, dst_block)` 2. `h2d_block(src_block, dst_block)` These two block-level KV transfer interface are needed for layerwise offload in prefill stage. 3. `d2h_token(src_token, dst_token)` 4. `h2d_token(src_token, dst_token)` These two token-level KV transfer interface are needed for sparse offload in decode stage. Since this topk loading time can not be overlapped with computing, we have high requirements for the bandwidth and latency of these two interface. Due to the high sparsity of topk KV distribution, it might be challenging to implement these token-level KV transfer operators. We are now trying to figure out if we can implement our layerwise & sparse KV offload based on existing offloading backends such as `OffloadingConnector` proposed in PR ([#22595](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/22595)) or `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` proposed in PR ([#37160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37160)). We notice that there are some significant differences between our offload approach and the existing ones: existing offload approaches are based on block-level offload & onload, mainly aim to enlarge prefix cache pool and improve prefix cache hit rate, while ours is based on both block-level and token-level offload & onload, mainly aims to save device memory usage and support larger batch size or longer sequence length. Due to the difference above, we may need to extend the existing offload backends. We may also consider to add a new offload backend for this sparse KV offload scenario if we find that the underlying data structure and loading process differ too large to combine together. ## Feedback Period. _No response_ ## Co-Authors. @ader47 @Angazenn @gjc0824 @grandolantow @LCAIZJ @LookAround0301 @luokui183 @wangxiaochao6 @wlwen1995 ## CC List. @LCAIZJ @ivanium ## Any Other Things. _No response_ ## Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC]: Standardize vLLM Entrypoint Error Handling
author: zqzten
body:
### Motivation.

As mentioned in #44303, currently vLLM entrypoint errors are fragmented and lack standardization. The root cause is that the codebase relies heavily on raw Python exceptions (`ValueError`, `TypeError`, `OverflowError`...) instead of semantic exception types — there are **2k+** `raise ValueError` across the codebase vs only **80+** `raise VLLMValidationError`.

This causes two concrete problems:

#### 1. Internal errors misreported as client errors (HTTP 400)

`AsyncLLM.generate()` treats all `ValueError` as request validation errors:

```python
except ValueError as e:        # "Request validation error"
    raise                       # → surfaces as HTTP 400

except Exception as e:          # everything else
    raise EngineGenerateError() # → surfaces as HTTP 500
```

Since `ValueError` is used indiscriminately — for client input validation, internal assertions, model execution errors, and config checks — any `ValueError` from any layer gets reported to the client as `400 Bad Request` instead of `500 Internal Server Error`.

#### 2. Prometheus metrics record wrong status codes

As identified in #44303, exceptions like `ValueError` propagate through the Prometheus middleware unhandled (caught by `ServerErrorMiddleware` outside Prometheus, not `ExceptionMiddleware` inside it), causing `http_requests_total` to record 4xx client errors as 5xx.

### Proposed Change.

#### Step 1: Extend the exception hierarchy

Add semantic base classes in `vllm/exceptions.py`:

```
VLLMError (new base)
├── VLLMClientError                    # 4xx — caused by the request
│   ├── VLLMValidationError            # 400 (existing, reparented)
│   ├── VLLMNotFoundError              # 404 (existing, reparented)
│   └── VLLMUnprocessableEntityError   # 422 (existing, reparented)
└── VLLMServerError                    # 5xx — caused by the server
    ├── EngineGenerateError            # 500 (existing, reparented)
    ├── EngineDeadError                # 500 (existing, reparented)
    └── GenerationError               # 500 (existing, reparented)
```

The key change is that `VLLMValidationError` currently inherits `ValueError`, but it should inherit `VLLMClientError` instead, breaking the dependency on `ValueError` for semantic dispatch.

`parameter`/`value` structured fields remain on `VLLMValidationError` and `VLLMUnprocessableEntityError` only (not on the base class), since other client errors like `VLLMNotFoundError` have no use for them.

Additional subtypes (e.g., `VLLMInternalError` for internal assertions, `VLLMNotImplementedError` for unsupported features) can be added in follow-up steps when there are concrete raise sites to use them.

#### Step 2: Migrate engine-layer `ValueError` to `VLLMValidationError`

Convert `raise ValueError` in the engine's request validation path to `raise VLLMValidationError`. Each site must be individually verified to confirm it represents a client input validation error, not an internal assertion. The sites identified so far:

- `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py` — 15 sites (prompt length/emptiness checks, task support checks, token ID range checks, multimodal input validation)
- `vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py` — 3 sites (config-request incompatibility: kv-sharing + prompt logprobs, streaming input constraints)
- `vllm/sampling_params.py` — 31 sites (`verify()`: temperature/top_p/top_k ranges, n >= 1, stop token validation, etc.)
- `vllm/pooling_params.py` — 10 sites (`verify()`: pooling parameter validation)

#### Step 3: Change engine catch to use semantic types

In `AsyncLLM.generate()` (both `generate` and `pooling` paths):

```python
# Before
except ValueError as e:
    raise

# After
except VLLMClientError as e:
    raise
```

After this change, only exceptions explicitly marked as `VLLMClientError` pass through as 4xx. Any unmarked `ValueError` from model execution or internal logic falls into `except Exception` → `EngineGenerateError` → HTTP 500. This is the **safer default**: a false 500 ("something went wrong, retry later") is less harmful than a false 400 ("your request is bad, don't retry").

#### Step 4: Simplify API-layer exception handler registration

In `api_server.py`, consolidate exception handler registration into three clear layers:

```python
# Before — flat list mixing framework, vLLM, and fallback handlers
app.exception_handler(HTTPException)(http_exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)(validation_exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(EngineGenerateError)(engine_error_handler)
app.exception_handler(EngineDeadError)(engine_error_handler)
app.exception_handler(GenerationError)(generation_error_handler)
app.exception_handler(VLLMValidationError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(VLLMUnprocessableEntityError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(VLLMNotFoundError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(ValueError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(TypeError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(OverflowError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(NotImplementedError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(Exception)(exception_handler)

# After — three layers: framework / vLLM / fallback (would gradually migirated to VLLMError except for Exception, see Step 5 below)
app.exception_handler(HTTPException)(http_exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)(validation_exception_handler)

app.exception_handler(VLLMError)(vllm_error_handler)

app.exception_handler(ValueError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(TypeError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(OverflowError)(exception_handler)
app.exception_handler(Exception)(exception_handler)
```

The unified `vllm_error_handler` dispatches to existing handler functions:

```python
async def vllm_error_handler(req: Request, exc: VLLMError):
    if isinstance(exc, (EngineGenerateError, EngineDeadError)):
        return await engine_error_handler(req, exc)
    elif isinstance(exc, GenerationError):
        return await generation_error_handler(req, exc)
    else:
        return await exception_handler(req, exc)
```

Update `create_error_response()` to dispatch on the new hierarchy, keeping the `isinstance(exc, (ValueError, TypeError, OverflowError))` → 400 fallback for unmigrated code.

#### Step 5 (follow-up): Migrate remaining raw exceptions in entrypoints

~135 `raise ValueError`, plus `TypeError`, `OverflowError`, and `NotImplementedError` in `vllm/entrypoints/` can be gradually converted in subsequent PRs:

- `ValueError` / `TypeError` / `OverflowError` → `VLLMValidationError` (these are request validation errors)
- `NotImplementedError` → a new `VLLMNotImplementedError(VLLMServerError)` with status 501, introduced alongside its first migration

These are caught by FastAPI exception handlers (not the engine catch), so the existing fallback handlers keep behavior unchanged until migrated. Once fully migrated, the `ValueError`/`TypeError`/`OverflowError`/`NotImplementedError` fallback registrations can be removed — any raw exception reaching the handler at that point is unexpected and should fall through to the `Exception` catch-all as a 500.

The `Exception` catch-all is a permanent safety net and should never be removed.

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@DarkLight1337 @noooop @markmc 

### Any Other Things.

#### PR Process

Steps 1–4 can be formed as a single atomic PR. Step 5 can be a series of follow-up PRs that can proceed incrementally without urgency. New exception subtypes (e.g., `VLLMInternalError`, `VLLMNotImplementedError`) should be introduced in those follow-up PRs alongside their first raise sites, not defined speculatively.

#### Backward compatibility

- **API behavior**: No change for correctly-typed errors. The only behavior change is that hypothetical `ValueError` from internal code paths (model executor, attention layers) would become 500 instead of 400 — this is a bug fix, not a regression.
- **`VLLMValidationError` inheritance**: Changing from `ValueError` to `VLLMClientError` breaks code that catches `ValueError` expecting to catch `VLLMValidationError`. Within vLLM, the only such site is the engine catch and would be fixed in Step 3. External users who depend on this inheritance are unlikely but would need to update their catch clauses.

#### This also resolves #44303

With `VLLMError` registered as a specific exception handler, all client errors are caught by `ExceptionMiddleware` (inside Prometheus middleware), ensuring correct status code recording without needing to register each exception type individually.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC] Speculative Decoding Lifecycle for RL Rollout
author: aoshen02
body:
# [RFC] Speculative Decoding Lifecycle for RL Rollout

## Problem

RL frameworks cannot use vLLM's speculative decoding (MTP / EAGLE / suffix) for rollout acceleration because:

1. **Config not exposed**: verl's `vllm.LLM` wrapper does not pass through `speculative_config` ([verl#4526](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/4526))
2. **MTP weight sync broken**: after RL training updates MTP head weights, `load_weights` does not reload MTP parameters — they go stale ([verl#6947](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6947))
3. **Draft model lifecycle**: EAGLE/EAGLE3 draft models need weight reload during sleep/wake, currently only verifier weights are updated ([#46725](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46725), already tracked in Section 1.1)

## Downstream demand

- [verl#5925](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/5925): EAGLE/EAGLE3 for RL rollout (verl PR, open)
- [verl#6342](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/6342): Suffix spec decode in vLLM rollout (verl PR, open)
- [verl#4791](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/4791): Suffix + LSTM spec decode RFC
- [SkyRL#1832](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/1832): MTP training support (P0 in SkyRL Q3 roadmap)

## Exit criterion

- verl can configure `speculative_config` for vLLM rollout without error
- MTP head weights correctly reload after `load_weights` / `finish_weight_update`

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

title: [RFC] LoRA Correctness and Lifecycle for RL Training
author: aoshen02
body:
# [RFC] LoRA Correctness and Lifecycle for RL Training

## Scope

Track unresolved vLLM LoRA issues affecting RL rollout correctness, adapter updates, and reliable execution. Prioritize silent policy/scoring errors and engine failures. Checked on 2026-10-15; completed fixes are omitted. An open fix is not evidence that the full issue is resolved.

## Correctness

- [ ] **MoE + DP adapter isolation:** #61453 — gathered tokens can lose expert deltas or receive another rank's adapter/version. PR #61714 addresses active-peer mapping/activation; fully idle peers and cross-rank slot consistency remain unresolved.
- [ ] **MLA adapter application:** #48974 — `kv_b_proj` LoRA is bypassed by absorbed decode and stale prefill references. PR #56718 covers prefill as part of composed MLA support; complete prefill/decode logprob parity remains to be validated.
- [ ] **Scoring consistency:** #51594 — `prompt_logprobs` omits `lm_head` LoRA despite generation using it. PR #51597 needs GPU validation of the candidate fix.
- [ ] **Speculative decoding isolation:** #59161 — Model Runner V2 maps `lm_head` LoRA per request instead of per logits row, dropping or cross-applying deltas. PR #59341.
- [ ] **Adapter loading must take effect:** #48019 — text PEFT adapters can silently match no modules on language-model wrappers. Shared mapping fix: PR #49525; GPU coverage is not yet complete across affected models.
- [ ] **Finite kernel outputs:** #48590 — Hopper `lora_expand` with `block_n=128` produces NaNs in reported H20 reproductions. PR #48638.

## Adapter Updates & Cache Identity

- [ ] **Same-path reload invalidation:** PR #48352 — changing adapter contents under the same name and path can retain stale prefix KV. Track the remaining content-versioning gap; the proposed local-file fix does not establish coverage for remote sources, shared-nothing deployments, or all external KV connectors.
- [ ] **Adapter-only synchronization:** [trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975) — support sending LoRA updates directly to vLLM without a merge/full-weight-transfer/unmerge round trip.

## Execution & Lifecycle

- [ ] **CUDA Graph / TP deadlock:** #60845 — fully-sharded MoE LoRA can deadlock when shared and routed experts issue collectives on different streams. PR #61284.
- [ ] **Large-prefill memory safety:** PR #59407 — int32 token-offset multiplication can overflow in MoE LoRA kernels, causing illegal memory access or corruption. FP8/TRT-LLM branches still need corresponding hardware coverage.
- [ ] **Pipeline-parallel scheduling:** #60301 — skipped running requests are omitted from adapter-slot accounting, allowing a later batch to exceed `max_loras` and crash EngineCore. PR #60306.

## Downstream Validation

- [ ] [SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776) — investigate rank-dependent LoRA training/inference mismatch on Qwen3.6 MoE and GLM-4.7-Flash. Keep this as a downstream validation case; attribution to the bugs above is not yet established.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Accepted adapter tensors take effect; unsupported targets/configurations fail explicitly. Generation and scoring match the intended adapter within justified numerical tolerances.
- Adapter identity and version remain isolated across mixed batches, DP ranks, speculative logits rows, and cache reuse after updates.
- Supported TP/PP, CUDA Graph, large-prefill, and repeated adapter-update configurations run without deadlocks, engine crashes, or invalid memory access.
- Adapter-only synchronization preserves these guarantees across repeated RL iterations. Record regression tests and hardware/model coverage in the linked implementation PRs.

## Feedback

Please attach reproductions and focused fixes to the corresponding checklist item; remove resolved items after verifying the fix covers the tracked scope.

title: [RFC] Training-Inference Consistency for RL
author: aoshen02
body:
# [RFC] Training-Inference Consistency for RL

**Anchors**: [#42259](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42259) (Logprobs), [#39568](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39568) (R3), [#45221](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45221) (Data Plane)

## Problem

RL training correctness requires that for the same sample, weights, and routing strategy, the trainer and rollout engine observe identical results. Eight consistency dimensions:

1. **Numerical consistency** — batch shape must not introduce avoidable numerical differences in inference; batch invariance is one component, not a complete trainer–inference parity guarantee.
2. **Logprobs & token-ID replay** — logprob mismatch → importance sampling ratio corruption → noisy policy gradient. `trace_decode_token_ids` ([#46701](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46701)) enables replaying a fixed token sequence while computing real logprobs.
3. **R3 routing replay** — MoE expert routing must be captured during inference and replayed during training. Mismatch → gradients computed on wrong experts.
4. **DSA index replay** — DeepSeek V3.2+ dynamic sparse attention indices must match between inference and training.
5. **Data plane** — logprobs, routed_experts, and DSA indices must be transported from inference GPU workers to trainer efficiently, bypassing the EngineCore/API Server bottleneck.
6. **Hidden states replay** — OPD requires exporting intermediate-layer hidden states from teacher to student, avoiding full `[tokens, vocab]` logit transfer.
7. **Dtype (logits precision)** — Inference must match training's fp32 precision for lm_head to maintain train-inference consistency.
8. **Per-request weight provenance** — each output token and its logprob must identify the model weight version that actually produced it, including requests that span an update boundary.

## Subsections

### 3.1 Numerical Consistency

Current batch-invariance tracker: [#27433](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433). Batch invariance is one component of training–inference numerical consistency, not a full parity guarantee.

### 3.2 Logprobs & Token-ID Replay

Full tracker: [#42259](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42259). Exit: #47680 + #42245 merged; #46701 accepted.

### 3.3 R3 Routing Replay

- [ ] [#44214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44214): FlashInfer + R3
- [ ] [#45419](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45419): P/D disagg + R3
- [ ] [#45635](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45635): KV offload + R3
- [ ] [#37094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37094): Align routed_experts with streamed output spans

Exit: R3 works on FlashInfer + P/D + KV-offload; R3 correctness test in RL CI.

### 3.4 DSA Index Replay

- [ ] [#47280](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47280): RFC — `--enable-return-indexer-topk`
- [ ] [#47279](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47279): Implementation

No downstream demand yet. Forward-looking for DeepSeek V4+ RL adoption. Exit: RFC accepted.

### 3.5 Data Plane

- [ ] [#47809](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47809): Artifact transfer connector (bypasses EngineCore/API Server bottleneck)
- [ ] [vime#320](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/pull/320): TransferQueue trajectory ingestion for closed-loop training

Exit: at least one data plane backend merged; R3 transport E2E verified.

### 3.6 Hidden States Replay

- [ ] [#37002](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37002): Observation Plugin — register plugins to intercept layer outputs via PyTorch hooks (Phase 1: API; Phase 2: model runner integration)

Exit: Observation Plugin Phase 2 merged.

### 3.7 Dtype Replay

- [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48390

### 3.8 Per-Request Weight Provenance

Merged [#49040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49040) adds an EngineCore weight-version label and query/update APIs. It does not bind a version to a request or token: querying the current version after generation cannot identify which weights produced earlier output.

Detailed design and background: [#54443](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54443), which defines per-output token spans and their capture, delivery, and boundary semantics.

- [ ] Return `weight_versions` as contiguous generated-token ranges `[start, end)` for each output sequence, with `model_id` at the sequence level; the ranges must cover every output token and its logprob exactly once.
- [ ] Stamp the version used by the target model step, not the version at response assembly or query time. A kept request that crosses a committed version change must return separate ranges for each version.
- [ ] Define the contract for streaming, speculative decoding, and DP replicas; test single-version output, a request crossing a successful update, and a failed update.

The version is caller-managed metadata, not proof that the supplied weights match a checkpoint. A metadata-only update must not be presented as evidence of a weight transfer.

## Feedback Period

Two weeks from posting.

title: [RFC] RL Information Retrieval: APIs & Introspection
author: aoshen02
body:
**Anchor**: [vllm#38147](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38147) (Runtime Data Endpoints)
**Related**: [vllm#45585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45585) (RL CI Matrix)

## Problem

---

## 2.1 RL Dev API Surface

- [x] [#47173](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47173): `POST /abort_requests` for dev RLHF API — frameworks need to discard oversampled generations at step boundaries
- [ ] [#45524](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45524): Prometheus pause state metric (`vllm:engine_pause_state`) — complements existing sleep state metric

Exit: #47173 + #45524 merged.

---

## 2.2 Weight Version Tagging

vLLM already has a `weight_version` counter hook point (`finish_weight_update`, [#39212](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39212), merged). CI docs contain `/weight_info` and `/update_weight_label` prototypes, but these have not been upstreamed to vLLM main. No standardized version tagging API exists across the ecosystem.

**Semantic conventions**:
- Version increments when `finish_weight_update` returns (i.e., after weights are fully written)
- In-flight requests bind to the **version at admission time** (locked when the request enters the scheduler queue)
- Single API server / single DP replica: monotonically increasing integer. Multi-replica: `(dp_rank, version)` tuple

Demand signals:

| Source | Issue | Ask |
|--------|-------|-----|
| vllm#31943 | [@h-avsha comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31943#issuecomment-3834098959) | "tracking weight versions... tagging llm responses with the corresponding version" |
| prime-rl | [#2812](https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-rl/issues/2812) | `TARGET_LAG=1` hardcoded — only framework with explicit version-lag mechanism |
| SkyRL | [#536](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/536) | Async RL tracker — requires in-flight weight update + version tracking |

- [ ] Draft RFC: weight-version tagging API (`weight_version` counter + response metadata)
- [ ] Weight version queryable via HTTP
- [ ] Version metadata injected into rollout responses

Exit: HTTP-queryable weight version + rollout response carries version metadata.

title: [RFC] Sleep/Wake Correctness for RL
author: aoshen02
body:
**Related RFCs:** [#48311](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48311) (engine lifecycle), [#48312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48312) (weight-update correctness), and [#48305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48305) (training-inference consistency).

## Problem

Sleep/wake must preserve liveness, memory ownership, model state, request state, and output correctness across every advertised model architecture and parallelism configuration. The bugs below were discovered by downstream RL frameworks or by vLLM RL lifecycle testing in production-like environments.

`SW1`–`SW6` below is the canonical root-cause taxonomy used by tests and the RL new-model support checklist.

## Scope and complete transition

This tracker owns sleep, wake, pause, drain, memory remap, and request/cache continuity. Weight mutation itself is owned by #48312. The combined RL transaction is:

```text
pause/drain -> sleep -> wake(weights) -> reload/update -> post-load/finalize
            -> wake(kv_cache) -> invalidate versioned caches -> resume
```

A 200 response proves only that an endpoint returned. Correctness requires the state and output oracles below before serving resumes.

## Root-cause taxonomy

| ID | Category | Required invariant | Minimum regression check |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW1 | Transition ordering and quiescence | No kernel, collective, scheduler step, or new request may touch memory whose required tags are unmapped; partial wake must not resume inference | in-flight decode + concurrent arrival + full/partial wake; synchronize all ranks; first post-wake request must complete |
| SW2 | Memory ownership, tags, and accounting | Every CUDA graph, weight, KV/SSM, LoRA, multimodal, offload, and communicator allocation is owned and unmapped/remapped exactly once | per-tag resident-byte accounting, repeated cycles, double-free/idempotency checks, TP/PP where declared |
| SW3 | State/value reconstruction | Remapped forward-visible state is initialized from an authoritative host/config value or explicitly zeroed before reuse; calibrated values must not be replaced by defaults | non-default sentinels for FP8 scales/buffers; poison discarded pages; compare fixed-token logits/logprobs before and after wake |
| SW4 | Heterogeneous state topology | Wake hooks traverse the actual state pytree, not an assumed flat `list[Tensor]`; Tensor/list/tuple/mapping/None/empty leaves are handled and unknown leaves fail explicitly | attention + hybrid Mamba/GDN cache trees, including TP/PP; recursive unit test plus real-model wake |
| SW5 | Cache invalidation symmetry | Paired caches and state held by different processes/layers are invalidated consistently; a sender must not claim a hit when the receiver was cleared | warm same-key prefix/MM/offload cache -> sleep/pause(clear) -> reuse -> assert both sides miss or both retain |
| SW6 | Request continuity | `abort`/`wait`/`keep` semantics preserve the exact promised request state; resume must neither drop nor duplicate tokens/logprobs | pause the same request at depth 0/1/N, resume, and compare token-by-token with an uninterrupted run |

## P0: Crash / hang

| Tracking | Root category | Bug | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#47700](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47700) | SW2 | CUDA graph memory is outside CuMem tracking, is not released, and causes OOM on wake | Open |
| [#45268](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45268) | SW2/SW3 | Native KV offload plus sleep kills the engine on the first cycle | Open tracking issue |
| [#36651](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36651) | SW2 | CuMem double-free and stale error codes across cycles | Open |
| [#48337](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48337) | SW2 | Level-2 sleep with LoRA leaves wrapped parameter names and stacked adapter state incompatible with reload | Open; also #48312 categories 4/6 |
| [#46371](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46371) | SW3/SW4 | FP8 scale initialization touches an unallocated tensor during wake | Open |

## Downstream reports

These are framework-side symptoms until a vLLM root cause is established.

| Issue | Framework | Mapping | Bug |
|---|---|---|---|
| [trl#5382](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5382) | trl | SW1/SW2 candidate | Colocation + TP + tool calling hangs in NCCL |
| [OpenRLHF#1162](https://github.com/OpenRLHF/OpenRLHF/issues/1162) | OpenRLHF | SW1/SW2 candidate | `--colocate_all_models` + TP>1 sleep crash |

## Required regression matrix

Every advertised feature combination gets the applicable rows; unsupported combinations fail closed and are documented rather than silently skipped.

| Axis | PR gate | Nightly / hardware lane |
|---|---|---|
| Sleep transition | level 1 and 2; full wake; weights-only then KV wake | reverse partial order, 20+ cycles, idempotent/repeated calls |
| Request state | idle plus one in-flight/new-arrival case | `abort`/`wait`/`keep`, async depth 0/1/N, speculative placeholders |
| Model state | dense baseline; every model-declared state type | MoE, hybrid Mamba/GDN, VLM, LoRA, speculative target+draft |
| KV state | default KV; FP8 if advertised | non-1.0 calibrated scales, native offload, poisoned discarded pages |
| Parallelism | TP=1; TP=2 if advertised | PP=2, DP/EP for advertised model paths, multi-node where supported |
| Cache state | cold and one warmed relevant cache | prefix, remote/offload KV, MM sender/receiver, hybrid recurrent state |

## Four mandatory oracles

1. **Output:** replay fixed token IDs and compare raw logits/logprobs before and after sleep/wake; generated text alone is insufficient.
2. **Liveness:** the first request and a second health request after wake must finish; an HTTP 200 followed by a dead worker fails.
3. **Memory ownership:** resident bytes and tag membership match the requested transition, no allocation is unmapped/remapped twice, and repeated cycles return to the same baseline.
4. **State/cache accessibility:** every required buffer, scale, KV/SSM state, and paired cache is initialized and mutually visible before scheduler resume.

## Composite RL E2E

At least one production entrypoint test must execute the whole transaction with different weight sets A and B:

```text
serve/capture A
-> pause and drain
-> sleep(level=2)
-> wake(weights)
-> update A to B through the production transfer path
-> post-load/finalize and #48312 checks
-> wake(kv_cache)
-> invalidate affected caches
-> resume
-> fixed-token logits/logprobs == cold-B engine
```

This catches interaction bugs that isolated sleep and isolated reload tests cannot catch.

## Exit criteria

- Every open P0 family above is fixed or the affected feature combination is rejected before transition.
- SW1–SW6 each have a regression using the mandatory oracle named in the taxonomy.
- Hybrid + FP8 KV covers recursive state traversal and non-1.0 scale restoration in nightly coverage.
- Discarded ordinary KV and hybrid SSM pages are initialized before first slot reuse.
- Pause/resume request continuity and multimodal sender/receiver cache symmetry remain covered by regression tests.
- The composite sleep/update/wake test jointly satisfies this RFC and #48312.
- The RL CI matrix runs for 30 days with no new correctness failure.

title: [RFC] Engine Sleep/Wake/Drain Lifecycle for RL
author: aoshen02
body:
## Correctness

Full sleep/wake correctness tracker: [#48310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48310). Weight-update correctness is tracked separately in [#48312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48312).

## Control Plane

Define the external `pause / drain / sleep / wake / resume` contract: request admission, quiescence, and what completion guarantees to callers.

- [ ] [#51476](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51476) — Define pause/sleep responsibilities, request admission, DP quiescence, and device-idle completion.
- [ ] [#51488](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51488) — Reject new requests during `abort`/`wait` pauses while preserving `keep` semantics.
- [ ] [#53082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53082) — Make sleep a memory-state transition with an explicit pause precondition.
- [ ] [#56754](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56754) — Drain in-process requests before sleep.
- [ ] [#58041](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58041) — Drain active KV receives during `pause(mode="keep")` without dropping retained KV or waiting for passive reader leases.
- [ ] [#53511](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53511) — Reset the MiniMax Lamport workspace before wake completes.
- [ ] Support `sleep(mode="wait")` in the in-process engine; it currently raises instead of draining running requests.

## Resource Management

Manage the internal mapping, release, restoration, and retention of GPU and host resources. Sleep/wake correctness details remain in [#48310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48310).

- [ ] [#36651](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36651) — Resolve CuMem double-release, mapping-state, and stale-error handling across sleep/wake cycles.
- [ ] [#57629](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57629) — Release cached pinned-host backup before a discarded wake remap on unified-memory systems.
- [ ] [#55206](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55206) — Optionally release pinned host memory after wake, trading host RAM for re-pinning cost on the next sleep.
- [ ] [#57810](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57810) — Optionally retain offloaded KV across pause/sleep **only when weights do not change**; a weight update must invalidate old-weight KV.

## Performance

| Tracking | Problem / goal |
|---|---|
| [#58183](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58183) | Experimental multi-worker CUDA process checkpoint: reclaim GPU-resident process state while preserving captured graphs. |
| [#57899](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57899) | Experimental level-1 graph discard and lazy recapture to reduce wake-to-serving latency. |
| [#34303](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34303) | Related CUDA checkpoint/restore design to retain graph and compile state across suspension. |
| [#48193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48193) | Related cold-start roadmap. |

## Other Features

- [ ] [#57011](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57011) — Add sleep/wake hooks for custom model loaders so external state tied to GPU memory can pause and resume.

## Exit Criteria

- Correctness: satisfy [#48310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48310) across the supported RL lifecycle.
- Pause/drain does not strand requests or KV transfers; sleep/wake preserves or invalidates external state according to the weight version.

## Problem

RL colocated execution must transition safely and efficiently between rollout, training, and resumed rollout, without stranding requests or leaking resources.

title: [RFC] Weight Reload Correctness for RL
author: aoshen02
body:
> **Revision 2 (2026-10-27).** This issue is the failure taxonomy. The fix path is direct reload ([#54477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477)), and each category below now names the PR that closes it. The storage-registry proposal (#48478) is closed: derived state is kept at its address by the code that derives it, not by a registry. Rev 1 is in the edit history.

## Problem

After a weight update, the engine must serve exactly what a fresh load of the new checkpoint would serve, with the cold-start CUDA graphs still valid. HTTP success is not evidence of this.

Failures are classified by root cause. One bug may break more than one invariant; it is tracked under its primary category.

## Scope

In scope: the update half of the RL transition, which is load and reload, post-load processing, state that must survive a reload, routing, name resolution, and caches made stale by an update. The sleep/wake half is tracked in [#48310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48310).

```text
pause/drain -> sleep -> wake(weights) -> update -> post-load -> wake(kv_cache) -> invalidate caches -> resume
```

## Taxonomy and status

PR numbers refer to the [#54477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477) tracker. ✅ means fixed on the validated branch, and the PR is being merged. ⬜ means open.

| # | Category | Invariant | How direct reload meets it | PRs | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Storage identity | An address captured by a CUDA graph or kept by a backend does not change across an update | Tensors are viewed back to checkpoint layout in their own storage; derived tensors are written back with `replace_parameter` | #58382, PR 5; check: F4, F5 | ✅ flagship backends; ⬜ checks |
| 2 | Runtime value refresh | Every derived tensor is recomputed from the new weights | Every module reruns its cold-start post-load processing; nothing is skipped | #58382, PR 5, PR 3 (expert padding) | ✅ |
| 3 | Loader lifecycle | Every write goes through the param's `weight_loader`, and post-load processing can run again | Post-load processing made rerunnable; direct writes routed through loaders | #57733, aoshen02/vllm#175, #61287 | ✅ flagship models |
| 4 | Reload state preservation | Parameters, buffers and model-level state needed by forward survive or are rebuilt | Parameters that post-load processing deletes or renames stay registered; model-level hooks rerun | #62407, #57733 | ✅ |
| 5 | Routing / sharding | Every tensor lands in the right parameter, rank and shard | The model's own `load_weights` routes every update, as at cold start | (no new mechanism) | ✅ TP, PP, EP, multi-node runs |
| 6 | Name / key mapping | Required names are all delivered; none is silently skipped | Contract: send every module whose post-load processing changes its layout | F2, F3 (#49090) | ⬜ |
| 7 | Cache coherence | A cache derived from weights N is invalidated or re-keyed before N+1 serves | Static sink KV is rewritten on update | #57733 (sink); others open | ⬜ partial |

## 1. Storage identity

Kernel constants, `1/a_scale`, absorbed MLA weights and decode copies used to be reallocated on every post-load pass, while captured graphs kept reading the old storage. Same-weight tests cannot see this: stale storage still holds bit-identical values until it is reused. The fix is local to each site, which writes back with `replace_parameter`. The sites fixed in PR 5:

- MoE kernel constants for TRTLLM, FlashInfer CUTLASS and CuteDSL (gpt-oss, MiniMax, Beam);
- NVFP4 activation gscales;
- Kimi-K3 decode copies and MLA inverse scales;
- GLM-5 indexer and KDA caches;
- drafter caches.

Earlier tracked items:

| Tracking | Component | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [#49789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49789) | Backend-owned tensors | Open; superseded by PR 5 for the sites above |
| [#50521](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50521) | FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE constants | Open; covered by PR 5 |
| [#50538](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50538) | FlashInfer B12x MoE | Open; not covered (SM120) |
| [#56570](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56570) | FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE | Open |
| [#48539](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48539) | Machete `act_perm` | Open; not covered |

## 2. Runtime value refresh

Checks must change the weights. The trainer perturbs the checkpoint, a second engine cold-starts on the same perturbed checkpoint, and every parameter, buffer and tensor attribute must be bit-identical between the two. This holds for these classes:

- BF16 dense and hybrid;
- FP8 block + MLA;
- NVFP4;
- MXFP4 + SWA;
- FP8 MLA + vision MoE.

Expert padding has to be zeroed on every load (PR 3). Without it, DeepSeek-V4.1 leaves stale bytes in the padded expert tiles after the update.

| Tracking | Component | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [#53509](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53509) | MoE derived buffers | Open; same goal as PR 5 |
| [#57638](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57638), [#56298](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56298) | KDA merged convolution | Open; covered by PR 5 |

## 3. Loader lifecycle

A write that bypasses the param's `weight_loader` (`param.data.copy_`, `default_weight_loader` on a param that has its own loader) is invisible to a reload. Direct reload runs every module's post-load processing at finish, so element-count completion accounting is not needed.

| Tracking | Failure | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [#61287](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61287) | gpt-oss experts and 6 multimodal models write around their loaders | Open, approved |
| aoshen02/vllm#175 | Muse Spark fused QKV, Inkling experts | Open |
| [#42821](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42821) | Stale `weight_loader` after `_setup_kernel()` (unquantized FlashInfer MoE) | Open |
| [#55198](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55198) | TensorizerLoader skips post-load processing | Open; fixed in #57733 |

## 4. Reload state preservation

| Tracking | Failure | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [#62407](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62407) | Params deleted or renamed by post-load processing cannot be found by the next load | Open |
| [#53741](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53741) | ModelOpt fused MoE runtime state | Open |
| [#57163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57163) | Calibrated KV scales lost across level-2 sleep | Open (#48310) |
| [#52479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52479) | Draft weights not reloaded after level-2 wake | Open (#48310) |

## 5. Routing / sharding

| Tracking | Failure | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [#56689](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56689) | Tied trainer names dropped before TP/PP transfer | Open |

## 6. Name / key mapping

With direct reload, an omitted module whose post-load processing changes its layout gets that processing applied to stale bytes. F2 makes this fail before any processing runs:

```python
required = names fed to load_weights at cold start - rotary caches - is_unused_checkpoint_weight
missing  = required - delivered      # at finish, before any post-load processing
```

| Tracking | Failure | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [#49090](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49090) | MTP completeness checked per bucket instead of per update | Open (F3) |

## 7. Post-update cache coherence

Any cache derived from model version N must be invalidated, or keyed by a new version, before N+1 serves. Static sink attention KV is rewritten on update (#57733). Prefix KV, multimodal encoder caches, LoRA caches and draft state still need per-feature handling.

| Tracking | Failure | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [#44950](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44950) | Same-name LoRA reload reuses stale multimodal encoder-cache embeddings | Open |

## Cross-cutting API and transfer correctness

| Tracking | Boundary | Required behavior |
|---|---|---|
| [#57853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57853) ([fix #57854](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57854)) | Invalid session or mid-reload failure | Reject updates while weights are asleep; a failed update must not report success |
| [#55781](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55781), [#55228](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55228), [#57022](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57022) | HTTP outcome, concurrent updates, XPU | Surface failures; never silently no-op |
| [#52235](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52235), [#57665](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57665) | Packed transfer | Exact round-trip of scalars and mixed-dtype slices |
| [#57130](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57130) ([fix #57131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57131)) | Sparse NCCL patches | Preserve non-contiguous indices and values |
| aoshen02/vllm#174 | NCCL receive memory | Release cached receive buffers after an update |

## Downstream reports

Being listed here does not assign the root cause to vLLM.

| Report | Path | Category |
|---|---|---|
| [verl #6256](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6256) | Megatron-Bridge LoRA → vLLM IPC | 6 |
| [TRL #7085](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7085) | Colocated FP8 → vLLM | 2–4 |
| [TRL #7200](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7200) | Weight sync, stale image encoder embeddings | 7 |
| [ROLL #500](https://github.com/alibaba/ROLL/pull/500) | HF weights → vLLM target/drafter | 6 |
| [SkyRL #1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776) | Megatron LoRA → vLLM rollout | unclassified |
| [OpenRLHF #621](https://github.com/OpenRLHF/OpenRLHF/issues/621) | Multi-node NCCL broadcast | unclassified |

## How each claimed model is validated

1. **Same weights, 3 updates.** Every tensor must equal its pre-update value (diff 0), and GSM8K before and after must match within 1 point (chat API for chat models). Covers categories 1, 3, 4 and 5.
2. **New weights (perturbation).** The trainer perturbs the checkpoint, and a second engine cold-starts on the same perturbed checkpoint. Every parameter, buffer and tensor attribute must be bit-identical between the updated engine and the cold-started one. Covers category 2, which same-weight runs cannot see.
3. **Multi-node and parallelism.** TP across nodes, TP × PP (Hy4, 4 nodes), and EP MoE. Covers category 5.

Per-model results are in [#54477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477).

## Exit criteria

- Every claimed model passes checks 1–3 on the merged PR stack.
- Categories 6 and 7 have their follow-ups merged (F2, F3, cache invalidation).
- The checks run in RL CI for 30 days without a new correctness failure.

title: [RFC]: fp8 KV cache for the Ampere sparse-MLA path (TRITON_MLA_SPARSE) via software dequant
author: nickus
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**`TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` (#47629) is bf16-KV-only, and on 24 GB cards that is the binding constraint.** I have a working sm_80/sm_86 fp8 KV path and would like to know whether the project wants it before I polish it into a mergeable PR.

#### The gap, in the PR's own words

`TritonMLASparseBackend` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/triton_mla_sparse.py`):

```python
supported_kv_cache_dtypes: ClassVar[list[CacheDType]] = ["auto", "float16", "bfloat16"]
```

its decode entry point is literally `_forward_bf16_kv`, and the base it inherits refuses quantized KV outright (`xpu_mla_sparse.py:238`):

```python
if is_quantized_kv_cache(self.kv_cache_dtype):
    raise NotImplementedError("FP8 kv is not supported with XPU MLA Sparse yet")
```

The stated reason fp8 is excluded on Ampere is that Triton cannot handle `fp8e4nv` there. That is true for **native** fp8 — and irrelevant for fp8 **as storage**.

#### The technique is already in this very PR

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/mqa_logits_triton.py:191`, added by #47629 itself:

```python
# Kernel decodes FP8 from uint8 via LUT (SM80 Triton can't load fp8e4nv).
```

The indexer already reads fp8 pages on SM80 by loading them as `uint8` and decoding in-register. **The KV path simply hasn't had the same treatment.** (`models/deepseek_v4/xpu/xpu_sparse_decode_fp8.py` does the same thing for XPU: *"dequantize FP8 KV cache pages to BF16 on the fly, then reuse the BF16 sparse MLA attention kernel"*.) So the precedent is accepted in-tree, twice, and neither conflicts with #43914 / #47060's "native FP8 requires SM89+" — software dequant is a different mechanism.

#### What I did

An `IS_FP8: tl.constexpr` branch inside **your own** `_sparse_mla_compute_tile` — the single function through which both `_sparse_mla_kernel_final` and `_sparse_mla_kernel_split` load KV — so fp8 inherits your split-KV, your merge kernel, your autotune and your masking for free. The standard 656-byte `fp8_ds_mla` page is loaded as raw `uint8` and decoded with bit-math that is **bit-exact vs `torch.float8_e4m3fn` over all 256 byte values**. Nothing about the cache layout changes; the existing C++ `concat_and_cache_ds_mla` writer already runs on sm_86 unmodified (`ENABLE_FP8` is CUDA-version-gated, not arch-gated — verified by execution).

Patch (224 lines, applies to `bbe2ab4d6`, one flag / one branch / one dispatcher arg): https://github.com/nickus/vllm-fp8kv/blob/main/patches/triton_mla_sparse_fp8.patch

#### Measured on RTX 3090 (sm_86) — including the part that is not good news

| | |
|---|---|
| fp8 dequant, all 256 byte values | **bit-exact** vs `torch.float8_e4m3fn` |
| Decode vs fp32 reference, through vLLM's **own C++ `ds_mla` writer** and **own `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`** | **cosine 0.999996** |
| KV pool capacity | **1.756×** (656 B vs 1152 B/token); **~1.63×** effective once the indexer's own K-cache is counted |
| Decode speed vs bf16, same kernel, bs=8 / topk=2048 | **0.92×** |
| Decode speed vs bf16, same kernel, bs=32 / topk=2048 | **0.45×** |

**So this is a capacity-for-speed trade, not a free win**, and I would rather say so up front than have it found in review. At bs=32 fp8 decode is currently ~2.2× slower. My working hypothesis is that the autotune *config lists* (`_FINAL_AUTOTUNE_CONFIGS`: `BLOCK_N=16` only; `_SPLIT_AUTOTUNE_CONFIGS`: `BLOCK_N=32` only) are tuned for bf16's 1152 B rows and that fp8's 656 B rows plus a scale load want larger blocks — but **I have not measured that on the real kernel yet**, so I am flagging it as a hypothesis, not a finding. On a 24 GB card the 1.76× capacity may well be worth the decode cost; on an A100 it plainly is not, which is an argument for keeping this opt-in.

#### What is NOT done

* The patch above is **kernel-only** and therefore inert on its own: the backend still declares bf16-only dtypes, `get_kv_cache_shape` returns a 576-wide row for every dtype (fp8_ds_mla needs 656 — `flashmla_sparse.py` already handles this), and `_canonicalize_sparse_mla_kv_cache_dtype` maps `fp8_e4m3 -> fp8_ds_mla` only for FLASHMLA_SPARSE / SM120. I have that wiring working out-of-tree; it is ~40 more lines.
* **No engine-level boot yet.** All correctness numbers above are kernel-level. I have not yet run `LLM(..., kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3")` end-to-end and compared logits against a bf16 run.

#### The questions

1. Does the project **want** fp8 KV on the Ampere sparse-MLA path, given it buys ~1.76× KV capacity at a decode cost that is currently significant at larger batch?
2. If yes: kernel-only PR first (the diff above, dispatch dormant until the backend declares the dtype), or one PR including the backend wiring?
3. Any objection to the fp8-as-storage / software-dequant approach in the shared `_sparse_mla_compute_tile`, given `mqa_logits_triton.py` already does exactly this on SM80?

Happy to do the engine boot + logits parity and the config-list measurement before opening the PR — I just want to know the feature is wanted first.

---

*Unrelated bug found while working on this path, already filed: #48364 / #48366 (fully-masked leading index chunks NaN-poison `xpu_mla_sparse`).*

### Alternatives considered

* **Native fp8 (`fp8e4nv`) on Ampere** — impossible; that is the constraint the PR itself documents.
* **Dequantize whole pages to bf16 before the kernel** — what the XPU path does; costs a full bf16 materialization of the gathered KV, which throws away the bandwidth saving that is the entire point on a 24 GB card.
* **Keep bf16 KV and shrink the model instead** — what 3090/4090 owners do today; it is why GLM-5.2-class DSA models are effectively unusable at long context on consumer Ampere.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/vllm) users if needed.

title: [RFC]: Support SparDA-style decoupled Forecast projection for lookahead KV prefetch in sparse attention
author: Srinivasoo7
body:
### Motivation.

This RFC frames the two problems (PCIe bottleneck on offloaded KV, O(T²) selection cost), introduces SparDA's Forecast projection as the fix, cites the paper's reported speedups.

### Proposed Change.

(1) new Forecast projection in the model definition, one per GQA group, 
(2) lookahead block selection at layer N for layer N+1, 
(3) prefetch fired through the existing KVConnector path one layer early.

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@orozery 

### Any Other Things.

Feasibility:
This points to the DSA/lightning-indexer integration as proof that the attention-backend abstraction supports extra selector projections, and to the existing KVConnector async offload path plus RFC #38260 as the infra this would extend, not duplicate.

Open questions:
Whether the connector can be triggered a layer early today, where the Forecast projection should live architecturally, whether to build a generic lookahead-selector abstraction, and how to gate on checkpoint/model availability.


Related References:
https://github.com/NVlabs/SparDA
Related RFCs: #38260,  #19854

title: [RFC] Fail-Closed Graph Storage Contract for Weight Reload
author: aoshen02
body:
## Summary

Introduce one explicit `GraphStorageRegistry` contract for tensors whose storage is retained by CUDA/HIP Graphs or backend objects across weight reloads.

The invariant is:

> If a weight update returns success, every registered graph-visible logical slot still resolves to the captured storage with a compatible layout. Otherwise the worker remains paused and the update fails.

This RFC is the production-design follow-up to #48312. Category 1 (storage identity) is enforced at runtime. Categories 2–4 continue to use the production post-load lifecycle plus the cold-B vs warm-A→B differential oracle defined in #48312.

## Confirmed source topology

Current `main` has two distinct update paths:

```text
Worker.reload_weights()
  -> ModelRunner.reload_weights()
  -> no WeightTransferEngine call

Worker.update_weights()
  -> WeightTransferEngine.update_weights()
```

Therefore the storage contract cannot live only in `WeightTransferEngine`. The ModelRunner owns the registry and the common completion check.

## Runtime assumptions

Weight reload runs after inference has been paused and drained. No inference executes during reload. Existing CUDA/HIP Graph objects remain alive and retain captured device addresses.

Consequences:

- reload updates the live model directly;
- no shadow model;
- no full A/B copy of model weights;
- no rollback to A;
- a failed reload leaves the worker paused/unhealthy and requires full reload or restart;
- no graph replay resumes before validation succeeds.

## Ownership

```text
Backend/layer
  -> register graph-visible storage

CUDA/HIP Graph capture boundary
  -> ModelRunner.storage_registry.snapshot(graph_id)

Direct reload or WeightTransferEngine finish
  -> ModelRunner.storage_registry.check_or_raise(graph_id)
  -> invalidate required caches
  -> commit weight generation
  -> allow scheduler resume
```

There is no direct Graph Manager ↔ WeightTransferEngine dependency.

## Single registration mechanism

Production uses one discovery mechanism: explicit registration.

```python
register_graph_storage(
    owner=layer,
    name="moe.experts.a_strides",
    tensor=a_strides,
    attr_path="quant_method.moe_kernel.fused_experts.a_strides",
)
```

- Parameters and buffers are inserted by a framework adapter through the same API.
- Backend-owned runtime tensors, workspaces, derived weights, and opaque resources are declared through a stable `nn.Module` owner plus an explicit attribute path. The resolver follows the live object chain after reload and never closes over the old kernel/tensor object.
- Graph capture snapshots the registry.
- Production does not use `TorchDispatchMode` discovery.
- Production does not recursively walk arbitrary Python object graphs.
- A backend without a complete reload-storage contract does not support warm reload while captured graphs remain alive; the operation fails closed.

Object walking remains an offline audit/CI tool. It generates review candidates and never defines the production manifest.

## Registry record

Each record contains:

- stable logical name;
- weak storage reference;
- storage identity / data pointer;
- shape, stride, storage offset;
- dtype and device;
- resolver for the current logical slot;
- graph generation identifier.

`id(tensor)` is insufficient because multiple tensor objects share storage and `.data = ...` replaces storage without replacing the Python object.

## Check semantics

After reload and before resume:

```python
current = record.resolver()

if current is None:
    raise ReloadStorageMismatch("logical slot disappeared")
if storage(current) is not record.captured_storage:
    raise ReloadStorageMismatch("logical slot rebound")
if layout(current) != record.captured_layout:
    raise ReloadStorageMismatch("layout changed")
```

The check does not compare values. Value correctness uses a value-changing A/B differential test:

```text
cold load B
==
load A -> capture -> reload B -> replay existing graph
```

## Completion gate

Both direct reload and weight-transfer updates enter the same ModelRunner-owned completion gate:

```text
accelerator synchronize
-> run existing PWAL / registered backend finalizers
-> storage_registry.check_or_raise()
-> invalidate required caches
-> commit weight_gen
-> resume
```

`process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL) remains the standard mechanism for recomputing packed, transposed, quantized, and other derived runtime values. A small explicit reload finalizer is reserved for non-standard backend/expert objects that are outside the existing PWAL lifecycle.

## Distributed failure

Every rank checks its local registry. Any rank failure fails the collective update. No rank commits the new generation and no scheduler resumes after a peer reports a mismatch.

## CI

1. Registry unit tests: alive storage, expired storage, slot rebind, layout mismatch, graph generations.
2. Entrypoint coverage: direct `reload_weights` and IPC/NCCL `finish_weight_update` both execute the completion gate.
3. Historical red/green tests: #48251, #41670, #46009, and #48438.
4. Hardware replay: capture A, reload B, allocation pressure, replay the existing graph, compare with cold B.
5. A source audit test reports post-load tensor creation/rebinding sites that lack registration. Audit output is a candidate list, not a runtime oracle.

## Rejected designs

- **WeightTransferEngine-owned registry:** rejected because direct `Worker.reload_weights()` bypasses WeightTransferEngine.
- **Automatic dispatch discovery:** rejected because compiled and opaque backend state is outside that contract.
- **Runtime arbitrary object walk:** rejected because reachability does not prove graph use and object graphs contain caches, handles, locks, cycles, and temporary state.
- **Check before every replay:** rejected; the reload completion boundary is sufficient and adds no steady-state overhead.
- **Automatic recapture:** rejected; it hides a violated reload contract.
- **Warning-only behavior:** rejected; stale or dangling graph addresses are correctness failures.
- **Shadow-model staging and rollback:** rejected because inference is quiesced during reload and failed workers do not resume.

## Implementation plan

1. Add `GraphStorageRegistry` and CPU unit tests.
2. Add ModelRunner ownership and capture snapshot lifecycle.
3. Add one common completion gate for direct reload and WeightTransferEngine completion.
4. Register parameters/buffers through the framework adapter.
5. Migrate known graph-visible backend state, starting with MLA, Marlin/Machete, CUTLASS MoE, FlashInfer B12x, and RDNA3 scratch.
6. Add GPU capture/reload/replay lanes.
7. Enable strict support only for backends whose contract is complete; unsupported combinations fail before mutating weights.

## Exit criteria

- A successful reload never resumes with a missing, rebound, or layout-incompatible registered graph storage.
- Unsupported captured-graph reload combinations fail before weight mutation.
- Direct reload and all WeightTransferEngine paths share the completion gate.
- Historical category-1 failures turn red without their fixes and green with them.
- Cold-B and warm-A→B existing-graph replay agree for the supported backend matrix.

AI assistance was used to audit the call paths and draft this RFC. I reviewed the design and source relationships and can defend the proposal end to end.

title: [RFC]: Make Triton kernel unit tests hardware-agnostic and cover untested kernels
author: adobrzyn
body:
## Motivation

vLLM ships a large and growing set of Triton kernels (MoE, Mamba/SSD, GDN/FLA, KDA, linear/flash attention, INT8/FP8 quantization, normalization). Triton is portable by design and these kernels already run on non-NVIDIA backends for example  Intel GPU (XPU) builds compile and execute them through the same Triton path. However, the unit tests for these kernels do not reflect that portability and a large fraction of the kernels has no isolated unit test at all. Two concrete gaps:

- Tests are pinned to CUDA even when the kernel is not:
  Many kernel tests hardcode device="cuda", torch.set_default_device("cuda"), or call CUDA-only host APIs (torch.cuda.get_device_capability(), torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()). The result is that a pure-Triton kernel which runs correctly on ROCm/XPU is still untested there: the test either error with a CUDA-only call or are simply skipped

- Many kernels are only tested indirectly, or not at all:
  A number of kernels are tested through a high-level pipeline test (e.g. the Mamba-2 SSD chunk kernels are reachable only via mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen; several DeepGEMM EP-scatter/gather and GDN/FLA helper kernels have no dedicated test). When kernel like that has a regression, the failure surfaces far from its cause and is hard to localize.

We reviewed the Triton kernel surface and selected the kernels we consider most important: the ones on the hot paths of widely-used model families (MoE, Mamba/SSD, GDN/FLA, KDA, attention, INT8/FP8 quant, normalization). This RFC proposes a uniform, upstream-friendly way to close both gaps for those kernels and explains why new or modified tests belong in upstream rather than living separately, somewhere in a vendor fork.

## Proposed Change

Every PR targets one kernel (or one tightly coupled kernel family) and states, in its description, which kernel it covers and the rationale for the change. Two PR shapes:

### "Adjusted" — make an existing CUDA-pinned test hardware-agnostic

For tests that already exist but are CUDA-bound:

- Replace device="cuda" / torch.set_default_device("cuda") literals with current_platform.device_type.
- Replace a module-level CUDA skip with
  pytest.mark.skipif(not (current_platform.is_cuda_alike() or current_platform.is_xpu()), reason=...).
- Scope genuinely CUDA-only assertions (device capability, stream capture, CUDA-only C++ ops) behind current_platform.is_cuda() /  is_cuda_alike() so CUDA behavior is unchanged and other backends take the path they already support.

### "New" — add an isolated test where coverage is missing

For kernels with no dedicated test (or only indirect coverage):

- Add a standalone test that launches the kernel directly (the same way its production wrapper does) and validates it
- Parametrize over the shapes/dtypes/flags the kernel sees in production so the test exercises each compiled variant
- Make it device-agnostic from the start (current_platform.device_type, no CUDA-only guards) so it runs on CUDA, XPU, ROCm and any other HW or plugin out of the box, possibly other HW.

### Guarantees that keep this upstream-safe

- No source-behavior change on CUDA/ROCm:
  The handful of touched source files only guard CUDA-specific host calls behind a platform check; the CUDA branch is the original code path
- Pure-Triton, no kernel rewrites. No .cu/SYCL kernel is added or modified
- Same numeric. References are standard PyTorch; tolerances follow existing upstream precedent (e.g. ROCm already doubles bf16 atol for selective_state_update - we extend the same thing to XPU)
- The pattern is already upstream-accepted. It matches what was merged in tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py and tests/kernels/ir/test_layernorm.py and two PRs in this effort (#42736, #43307) are already merged upstream.
- Why these tests belong upstream and not in a fork:
    - The kernels are upstream and hardware-agnostic, so their tests must be too
    - Indirect coverage is not regression-localizing coverage
    - It strengthens upstream CI for everyone
    - One kernel per PR, each with an explicit rationale

### Scope

This scope covers the most important kernels: the ones used in key paths for widely used model families. They are grouped by function below, with representative PRs listed for each group (open unless noted):

| Group | Representative PRs |
| --- | --- |
| MoE | #43407, #44298, #45809 |
| Mamba / MambaMixer / SSD | #42736 (merged), #45016, #45140 |
| GDN / FLA | #44314, #44315, #44385, #45899, #45694, #47976 (draft as PR limit was reached) |
| KDA | #44982, #45694 |
| DeepGemm (EP scatter/gather, SiLU-mul) | #45921, #46061, #46064, #46128 |
| Attention (merge_attn_states, decode_attention) | #46134, #47862 (draft as PR limit was reached) |
| INT8 / FP8 Quant | #45382, #45694, #46073 |
| Linear / Lightning Attn | #43307 (merged) |

This approach has already been proven upstream: #42736 (Mamba kernels on two hardware backends) and #43307 (lightning_attn + AWQ Triton) have both been merged, with no CUDA regressions.

###

No compatibility impact is expected. CUDA and ROCm code paths and test results remain unchanged: the source edits only guard CUDA-only host calls behind a platform check, and each new test is either device-agnostic or XPU-only. There are no changes to public APIs, kernels, or numeric.

### Test plan

Each PR is validated on GPU and  Intel XPU (Battlemage). CUDA/ROCm continue to be covered by upstream CI, which the gated, additive tests do not alter.

title: [RFC]: Waiting-Queue-Informed LRU for Prefix Cache Eviction
author: chaunceyjiang
body:
### Motivation.



Automatic Prefix Caching (APC) currently evicts free cached KV blocks in LRU order. However, the eviction policy is unaware of demand from requests in the scheduler waiting queue.

Under KV-cache memory pressure, the allocator may evict a cached prefix that belongs to a request near the head of the waiting queue. If that request is admitted shortly afterward, the same prefix must be recomputed, reducing cache efficiency and increasing compute overhead and TTFT

The waiting queue already provides a useful short-term demand signal: requests closer to the head of the queue are generally more likely to be scheduled soon. The eviction policy can use this signal to preferentially retain cached prefixes that are likely to be reused in the near future.

The proposed behavior does not change request admission order, reserve additional KV-cache capacity, or pin blocks. It only changes the order in which free cached blocks are selected when an allocation would otherwise evict cached data.



### Proposed Change.



Introduce a **Queue-Informed LRU** policy for APC block eviction.

When a KV-block allocation would evict cached data under the ordinary LRU policy, the allocator performs the following steps:

1. Inspect up to the first `max_num_running_reqs` requests in the scheduler waiting queue.
2. Perform a read-only lookup of the local contiguous cached prefix for each inspected request.
3. Collect the matching block IDs into a temporary retained set.
4. Preferentially evict blocks that are not in the retained set.
5. If there are not enough non-retained blocks, fall back to evicting retained blocks in their original LRU order.

For example:

```text
Original LRU order: [A, B, C, D, E]
Retained block IDs:    {B, D}
Eviction order:     [A, C, E, B, D]
```

A retained block is not pinned. Retention only lowers its eviction priority for the current allocation. If additional capacity is required, retained blocks can still be evicted, ensuring that the policy does not cause an otherwise feasible allocation to fail.

To minimize scheduler overhead, retained-set construction is triggered lazily:

* If an allocation can be satisfied using free blocks that do not contain cached data, the existing fast path is used and the waiting queue is not inspected.
* The waiting queue is queried only when ordinary LRU selection would evict cached blocks.
* The retained set is resolved at most once during a single `KVCacheManager.allocate_slots` transaction and reused by all lower-level block allocations within that transaction.
* The temporary state is cleared when the allocation finishes, including when an exception is raised.

The waiting-prefix lookup must remain read-only. It must not modify block reference counts, LRU state, last-access metadata, cache-hit metrics, request block tables, or cache-access events.

The policy changes only which free block IDs are selected for eviction. Cache eviction, accounting, reference-count updates, and block allocation continue through the existing `BlockPool.get_new_blocks` path.


### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@njhill @ZJY0516 

### Any Other Things.

_No response_

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC]: Session-centric KV-cache orchestration over typed session identity
author: vMaroon
body:
### Motivation.

Agentic workloads are stateful programs, and their KV-cache is the program's working memory - tool definitions reused every turn, prefixes shared across parallel branches, context carried across turns and pauses. Serving them well across a fleet is a state-orchestration problem: which session state to keep, where to place it, when to move it, which program it belongs to. That orchestration belongs above the engine, in a control plane (llm-d, Dynamo) whose indexer becomes the cluster's memory map - while the engine stays a policy-unaware mechanism that materializes KV, reports what it did, and executes intent-free directives.

Typed session identity is the first primitive that split needs, and it is in flight: #48049 proposes a request-level `session_id` that engine internals and connectors read instead of overloading `request_id` or `extra_args`, with the implementation open in #48048. This RFC builds directly on it.

But `session_id` makes identity readable inside the engine; session-centric orchestration by an external control plane needs two more things the engine must expose and accept, both intent-free:

- Visibility in session coordinates. KV-cache events today report block hashes with no session or lineage. A control plane can read `session_id` on the request, but it cannot see which stored blocks belong to that session, or when they were evicted, without recomputing engine hashes — the coupling that makes the prefix-cache path mirror engine internals. Echoing the session coordinates on KV events closes that gap: the indexer maps KV lifecycle to sessions directly, no tokenization, no hash mirroring.
- Directives in session coordinates. Keeping a paused session warm — and later offloading, moving, or prefetching its state — are the actual orchestration actions. The retention API (#37003) is the first of them; it becomes addressable at session granularity once the coordinates exist on both the visibility and directive sides.

One coordinate is coarser than orchestration needs. `session_id` scopes a lineage; it does not locate a position within it, which is what fork-safe, recompute-stable KV addressing requires. This RFC adds a second, content-derived coordinate — `continuation_id`, a chain position whose equality holds exactly when content prefixes are byte-identical (same model, same `cache_salt`) — carried and echoed the same way, opaque to the engine.

The identity all of this rests on is already declared at the application edge and already plumbed by #48049: Anthropic Messages carries `cache_control` block markers and the conversation array; OpenAI Chat and Responses carry `prompt_cache_key`, `prompt_cache_retention`, `previous_response_id`, and conversation objects. The control plane sets `session_id` from those where present and derives it from content where absent; `continuation_id` is always content-derived, with declared ids aliasing into it. The engine parses none of it.

## Proposed Change.

The ask is small: a `continuation_id` request coordinate beside `session_id`, echoed with it on block-store events, and the directive channel aligned to the same coordinates. Everything else is framing and roadmap.

### Coordinates

- `session_id` (from #48049) — the session scope, constant across a session. Adopt as-is; no competing field.
- `continuation_id` — a content-derived chain position, the addressable node. Carried on the request beside `session_id`, opaque to the engine, recomputable by the control plane from any resent prefix. Proposed as a scalar field mirroring `session_id` — the minimal form; if #48049's `RequestMetadata` direction lands, it moves into that structure's "cache lineage" slot.

The two are orthogonal and both load-bearing. Being content-derived, `continuation_id` is identical across sessions exactly where their content is: a shared prefix, a fork's common ancestor. Neither `session_id` nor an engine-reported token offset can supply that — an offset locates a block within one request; a block shared by several sessions, or the same position reached by two of them, has no common name unless the name is the content.
